data.title: Various Projects Find Hidden SDR Capabilities in ESP32 Microcontrollers
data.author: nkw
data.article_summary: ESPARGOS团队发现，部分ESP32芯片具备未公开的IQ基带采样功能，可覆盖2.2–2.7GHz，ESP32-C5还支持4.8–6.0GHz，最高80MS/s，可作为频谱分析仪。ESP32-S31能经千兆网连续传输，未来支持GNU Radio等。该功能还使ESPARGOS可对任意2.4GHz信号进行测向。另有项目借助FPGA实现连续数据流，及C5VRX用于5.8GHz图传接收。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ESP32 芯片隐藏的原始 IQ 采样能力及其作为低成本 SDR（软件定义无线电）的应用、性能与限制。

不同观点：
• **应用前景乐观**：可用于 OpenTrafficMap，采集交通灯、车辆和传感器的 802.11p V2X 数据；也可能接收 S 波段卫星下行信号，服务教育、业余无线电及 13cm/5cm 频段实验。  
• **低成本教育价值**：有人认为这类不到数美元的芯片，能显著降低 SDR 教学和实验门槛；也有人将其类比为可改造成 SDR 的电视棒。  
• **硬件与性能期待**：ESP32-S31 的 1Gbps 接口可能便于导出 I/Q 数据，估计可达到 20–40MSPS；ESP32-S3 的调谐范围据称约为 2.2–2.8GHz。有人设想通过 PSRAM 或逻辑分析仪直接获取采样数据。  
• **技术限制与改进**：当前方案依赖 FPGA 为 ESP32 提供时钟，可能导致相位噪声较差；相关项目近期已有修复。数据传输、信号质量（相位噪声、镜像、直流偏置等）仍缺乏充分实测。  
• **合规与安全担忧**：芯片可能具备任意发射能力，但现有项目主要限制为只接收。评论担心若任意 TX 引发监管、认证或出口管制问题，厂商可能通过固件或硬件“封堵”该功能。  
• **其他设想与疑问**：有人询问能否利用其精确时序实现可靠的 LoRa 类系统；另有人观察到近期 ESP32 讨论增多，但不确定是否只是关注偏差。

补充讨论：争议核心在于“低价、稳定的 SDR 能力”与射频性能、数据导出难度及法规风险之间的平衡；目前不少结论仍属推测，需实物测试验证。

49922674.article_content:
Back in 2025,
we posted
about ESPARGOS, a phased array of many patch antennas, each connected to an ESP32 WiFi microcontroller. ESPARGOS could be used to determine the direction of arrival for WiFi signals and create a live augmented reality heatmap.
Recently, the ESPARGOS team has
made an exciting discovery
. They found that several ESP32 chips have an undocumented feature that lets the firmware bypass the fixed WiFi and Bluetooth functionality and instead capture raw IQ baseband samples. As a result, several ESP32 models can now be used as an internal SDR covering 2.2–2.7 GHz, plus 4.8–6.0 GHz on the ESP32-C5, with up to 80 MS/s sample rate and roughly 13–54 MHz of analog bandwidth, depending on the chip.
However, for use as a general-purpose PC-connected SDR, the output bandwidth is insufficient, so only snapshots of data can be exported to a PC. This means that the SDR will only work as a spectrum analyzer, and demodulating or decoding continuous radio data is not possible with just an ESP32. The exception is the new ESP32-S31, which can stream continuously at up to 16 MS/s over its Gigabit Ethernet interface, with a SoapySDR driver for GNU Radio and gqrx coming soon. If you want to try it yourself, the ESP-WebSDR page lets you flash the firmware to most ESP32 dev boards directly from your browser and view a live spectrum and waterfall.
Furthermore, ESPARGOS notes that phase-coherent IQ sample capture is now possible with their hardware. This means ESPARGOS is no longer limited to WiFi and Bluetooth signals; it can now perform direction finding on any arbitrary signal in the 2.4 GHz band. The team also says phase-coherent transmissions would be possible, but they aren't implementing them right now because they could be misused.
It also seems that, independently, at least two other projects discovered the same or similar features around the same time, but to solve different problems.
Over on Reddit,
user /u/h0m3us3r discovered the same feature
and uploaded it to GitHub on Sept 26, and recorded a video showing an ESP32-S3 working as an SDR with an FPGA used as a USB3 front end. Unlike ESPARGOS, h0m3us3r's project streams the raw IQ data to a PC continuously via the FPGA rather than in snapshots, so full demodulation/decoding on PC should be possible. However, the current prototype uses the FPGA to clock the ESP32, which results in poor phase noise. So if the clocking issues can be resolved, an ESP32 combined with an FPGA could make a standard general-purpose SDR, like the RTL-SDR, but with a 2.2–2.8 GHz frequency range and up to 80 MHz of bandwidth.
Another project that seems to be using a somewhat similar finding is
C5VRX
, which was first uploaded to GitHub on August 13. C5VRX uses an ESP32-C5 as a 5.8 GHz real-time FPV video receiver. Although this project appears to use a different mechanism, the result is similar: it uses an undocumented IQ data stream on the ESP32 to sample FPV signals and demodulate them onboard, outputting analog composite video through a simple resistor DAC. The project is still a work in progress and doesn't yet work reliably at range.

data.title: SvelteKit 3
data.author: sampsn
data.article_summary: SvelteKit 3.0正式发布，整体延续此前框架体验，并提升了代码类型安全性、配置简洁度和错误处理能力。官方提供sv migrate命令，帮助迁移旧项目并生成待办清单；新项目可用sv create创建。主要变化包括配置迁移至vite.config.ts、$lib改为#lib、更强大的环境变量支持及更简洁的Service Worker。远程函数仍在开发中，预计需配合实验性Async Svelte使用。下届Svelte Summit将于11月在卢布尔雅那举行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Svelte/SvelteKit 新版本的价值、开发体验，以及在 AI 编程时代与 React、Vue、Solid 等方案的比较。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为 Svelte 更接近原生 HTML，代码可读性和开发体验好；SvelteKit 生产稳定、渐进改进，stores、双向绑定等功能简化开发，且比 Next.js 更令人愉悦。  
• Rich Harris 认为即使代理生成代码，框架仍影响最终质量：Svelte 可减少 JS 体积和 SSR 耗时，并重视可访问性、渐进增强；更高效的框架也能减少 AI token 消耗。  
• 多位用户表示现代 LLM 已能较好生成 Svelte 代码，配合 svelte-check 可快速完成项目；但也有人询问其“氛围编程”体验是否真的优于 React。  
• 反对或保留意见认为，Svelte 的自定义语法带来沉重的工具维护成本，JetBrains 插件支持差，开发者被迫依赖 VS Code；因此有人转向基于标准 TS/TSX 的 Solid。  
• 有人批评 Svelte 频繁“重新发明轮子”、版本变化大，也质疑 SvelteKit 的“+page.svelte”路由命名和嵌套目录设计。

补充讨论：案例显示 Svelte 可用于网站、桌面和移动端，Wails 下生成的应用体积小于 20MB。讨论还涉及全栈单体是否优于前后端分离，以及社区对 React、htmx 和破坏性升级标准不一致的质疑。

49926536.article_content:
Version 3.0 of SvelteKit, the official application framework for Svelte, is now available.
If you’ve used earlier versions of SvelteKit, everything will feel very familiar — it’s the same framework with a little more polish, a little more type safety, and a little less junk. We’ve made migration as seamless as we can with the
sv migrate
command...
npx
sv
migrate
sveltekit
-
3
--
tasks
all
--
confirm
...which will automatically migrate as much of your codebase as possible, and generate a TODO list for everything else. (If you’re agentically inclined, your robot friends will make short work of it.)
To create a
new
app, run
sv create
:
npx
sv
create
my
-
new
-
app
As with any major version bump there are a handful of breaking changes to be aware of, which are covered in the
migration guide
(or, more briefly, in the recent
release candidate announcement
).
Quick highlights:
configuration now lives in
vite.config.ts
instead of
svelte.config.js
the
$lib
alias is now
#lib
, making use of standard
subpath imports
environment variables
are more powerful and easier to use
service workers
are less boilerplatey
error handling is improved across the board
Are remote functions ready yet?
Not quite. But it’s our top priority!
Remote functions
are a set of utilities for secure, efficient, type-safe client-server communication. You’ve likely seen some version of this idea in other frameworks, but we think you’re going to prefer this one.
Using them requires
Async Svelte
, which for now requires an
experimental
flag. Bear with us.
Join us in Ljubljana next month
This is as good a place as any to remind everyone that the next in-person
Svelte Summit
is taking place on November 19-20 in the lovely town of Ljubljana, Slovenia. Among other things it will be a celebration of Svelte’s 10th birthday, and we’d love to share some cake with you.

data.title: CSS Bed: Classless CSS themes to use as starting points in web development
data.author: sea-gold
data.article_summary: CSS Bed 是一个收集无类（classless）CSS 主题的网站，可作为网页开发起点。用户只需将主题代码粘贴到 HTML 的 `<head>` 中即可使用。主题种类丰富，具备响应式、浏览器兼容性好、体积小、无需学习复杂类名等特点。页面还展示了表单、代码、表格、排版、链接及各类 HTML 元素效果，并提供 GitHub 源码和主题贡献入口。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“无类（classless）CSS/极简 CSS 框架”作为网页开发起点的实用性、默认样式质量及发展趋势展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持无类 CSS：认为仅依靠 HTML 元素即可快速获得可用页面，适合作为起点；Pico.css、simple.css、tacit、w3c-chocolate、Bootstrap 等被认为能提供可靠基线，甚至可约束 LLM 生成过度复杂的 CSS。  
• 质疑“无类”限制：一旦需要细微布局调整，就必须引入类或其他非元素选择器；对于多页面项目，matcha.css 等贴近原生元素、但保留扩展能力的方案更实用。  
• 倾向自建可扩展方案：有人采用 reset.css、var.css、global.css、util.css、markdown.css 分层组织纯 CSS，以兼顾简单性和规模化。  
• 认为现有默认值不够好：不少主题在移动端缺少左右边距、导致横向滚动；字体排版、标题与段落间距等基础细节也常不合理。  
• 功能期待：dark mode 被认为应成为现代“合理默认值”；用户还希望能直接滚动浏览主题，而非逐个切换。  
• 现状与趋势：有人已多年使用 Tailwind，询问 normalize/reset.css 是否仍主流；也有人认为无类 CSS 可能借助 LLM 重新流行。

补充讨论：评论者还分享了 drop-in CSS、HTML3000 等类似项目，并指出个别链接存在异常跳转。

补充讨论：评论者还分享了 drop-in CSS、HTML3000 等类似项目，并指出个别链接存在异常跳转。

data.title: Several vulnerabilities have been discovered in the Linux kernel
data.author: luispa
data.article_summary: Debian于2026年9月29日发布安全公告DSA-6528-1，针对linux软件包修复大量安全漏洞，涉及2024至2026年公布的数百个CVE，可能影响内核及相关组件安全。建议Debian用户及时更新linux软件包，以降低攻击风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI加速软件漏洞发现后，开源项目和整个计算基础设施如何应对，以及CVE数量是否能真实反映安全风险。

不同观点：
• 乐观者认为，AI让更多人看到长期隐藏的问题，虽短期造成项目维护压力，但建立筛选、人工复核和定期修复流程后，能提升软件质量。小型项目称每月发现22个漏洞并可及时修复。  
• 悲观者认为，AI编程并未显著降低漏洞率，却大幅提高代码产量和安全研究速度，未来漏洞会持续激增，暴露计算基础设施的脆弱性。  
• 有人指出，AI生成“能运行”的代码与“安全”的代码之间存在明显差距；安全具有成本，若缺乏实际责任，软件公司往往不会主动承担。  
• 另一派质疑以CVE数量衡量问题：Linux对几乎所有可能影响内核安全的缺陷都谨慎分配CVE，因此“1313个漏洞”或CVE编号突破十万并不等于同等数量的严重漏洞。  
• 有评论要求补充漏洞是否可远程利用、是否仅本地提权等关键信息，认为单报数量不足以判断风险。

补充讨论：争议焦点是AI究竟主要带来安全收益还是风险扩张，以及人类过去未发现大量漏洞是否反映人工审查能力不足。评论还提到项目规模、代码质量与维护团队难以线性扩展，并建议统一版本规则，用不同版本号区分安全补丁、功能和系统性变更。

data.title: Using Opus 5.5 to discover a new eyewitness record of the dodo
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕大语言模型（LLM）在历史研究、资料处理、跨学科创新中的能力、局限及实际价值展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **效率与规模化研究价值**：Twiin称Opus 5.5处理了逾1万张二战档案图片，辅助破解1941年未破译的武装党卫军密码，并快速编写多个解码器；其价值在于跨语言处理和大幅降低研究成本，而非发现密码新漏洞。  
• **能力强但错误难以预测**：nl指出模型能完成高难度任务，却会犯“整体合理、局部错位”的非人类式错误，也不擅长判断发现的历史意义；并质疑文中表现是否属于较早版本。  
• **适合整理个人与冷门史料**：jamienk考虑扫描父亲的大量日记交给模型分析，体现人们希望借助AI挖掘未被理解的私人资料。  
• **对研究成果规模的质疑**：early_exit追问文本总页数，认为若仅从约3000页中找到渡渡鸟资料，筛选本身可能比发现内容更值得称道。  
• **跨学科促进新想法**：SV_BubbleTime赞同模型处于学科交界时更容易产生创新，类似让铁匠与面包师知识结合以改进炉子。  
• **补充性知识讨论**：Neil44纠正渡渡鸟仅生活在毛里求斯；dgellow则肯定文章质量。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于AI究竟带来真正的研究突破，还是主要充当高效的资料整理、转录与筛选工具；其结论仍需人工验证。

data.title: Pi Durable
data.author: paulsmith
data.article_summary: Earendil与Pi社区发布Pi 1.0，并推出实验性框架Pi Durable。它不取代编码代理，而是用于构建可长期运行、跨环境、支持多人协作的智能体应用。该框架以存储和任务执行为核心，支持内存、SQLite、JSONL等后端及本地或远程执行环境，具备持久对话、故障恢复、上下文压缩和高度可定制等特点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Pi Durable 及类似“持久化 Agent harness”的架构、价值、实现难点与应用场景展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **看好持久化与云端迁移**：vito 介绍 Dagger agent，通过 OpenTelemetry 记录可重放的函数配方，使多沙盒状态可恢复、跨本地与云端迁移，支持长期、多 Agent、手机远程协作；lukebuehler 认为该方向具备耐久运行、故障恢复、监控、安全扩展和多人协作优势，行业正在趋同。
• **质疑状态一致性**：pulkitsh1234 关注 Agent 检查点与 VM、容器、浏览器等运行器状态如何同步；若 Agent 恢复但外部环境未恢复，可能产生“记忆已完成、实际未完成”的错位。
• **讨论数据模型取舍**：lemming 质疑 Durable 不支持真正的分支对话树，仅保留带祖先信息的 fork，认为这可能限制原有 Pi 能力，并追问是否是持久化保证所必需。
• **关注存储与外部系统整合**：vmg12 希望 JSON 文档之外支持 outbox 模式；rsalus 讨论 JSON/SQLite 持久化与内存方案的取舍，并希望加入沙箱策略引擎。
• **谨慎评价复杂度与实际用途**：ernsheong 认为多实例协调已很复杂，新增系统未必值得；phainopepla2 追问无限运行 Agent 的真实用途。ice3 则认为 Git、worklog 已能实现较简单的恢复。
• **其他反馈**：有人最看重多用户和远程控制；也有人质疑“harness”定义及云存储依赖，并讨论 token 统计差异、项目命名来源。

补充讨论：Durable 被视为 Dots、Deep Agents 等“常驻数字员工”产品的一部分；整体仍处实验和快速演进阶段。

49925969.article_content:
Pi Durable
Date:
Thu, 01 Oct 2026
From:
Earendil Engineering <
rfc@earendil.com
>
To:
You
Subject:
Pi Durable
Today Earendil and the Pi community
shipped Pi 1.0
. This
reflects our belief that after countless hours of hardening, maintenance, and
active development, Pi is now a solid foundation on which to build. Pi also
continues to evolve. Together with Pi 1.0, we are shipping an experimental new
package called Pi Durable. Pi Durable was built specifically for long-running,
durable, and malleable agents that can run anywhere. We would like you to join
in the fun and help us make it the best durable harness there is.
Why Pi Durable?
Pi the coding agent is built to run on your (remote) machine, inside a terminal,
driven by one person. If the process dies, you look at what happened and tell it
to continue. That is what Pi 1.0 focuses on and excels at, and that is not
changing.
At Earendil, we want to bring this technology to everyone, in whatever form fits
their needs best. For that, we need a harness that runs anywhere, can be reached
from different surfaces, supports infinitely long conversations, survives
catastrophic internal and external failures, and lets multiple humans steer the
same agents.
Pi Durable is that harness. It does not replace the Pi coding agent. It is a
framework for building any agentic application, coding agents included. It
shares not only code with the Pi coding agent, like pi-ai, but also its
principles: minimalism and malleability.
It also lets us explore designs in this space without disrupting Pi the coding
agent. Lessons we learn building agentic applications on Pi Durable will flow
back into Pi the coding agent as they prove themselves valuable.
What is a harness?
Everybody has their own definition of a harness. We
wrote about this
previously
, but let us reintroduce the concept of
the harness for Pi Durable.
A harness is storage plus the machinery needed to run one or more conversations
with large language models in parallel. It provides the tools those models call,
and the execution environments the tools run in.
A conversation is an interaction between you and an agent, recorded as a
transcript. The agent is the large language model together with its settings,
like the thinking level, and the tools it can call.
Tools do their work through an execution environment, which can be your laptop,
a remote VM, or an in-memory sandbox. Which tools and which execution
environment an agent gets is up to each conversation.
Everything the harness runs, from calling the model to executing a tool, is a
task.
Like everything in Pi, Pi Durable is built so your agent can understand it. The
entire source code, without tests, is about 15,000 lines, which comes out to
about 150,000 tokens with GPT and about 250,000 with Claude. That's the worst
case. To build on Pi Durable, your agent rarely needs all of it; the storage
backends alone are 3,000 lines it can usually skip.
Now let us give you a little tour of Pi Durable, to illustrate what we built and
why we built it.
Long runs anywhere
We want agents to run for a long time and to be able to run anywhere, where
anywhere currently means anywhere there is a JavaScript runtime.
In Pi Durable, a harness opens over a storage backend. Pi Durable ships memory,
SQLite, and JSONL storage, plus a conformance suite and benchmarks for your own
backend. The SQLite and JSONL storage code uses no Node APIs, so with a small
adapter it runs on Bun or inside a Cloudflare Durable Object. The storage
interface is small and easy to implement on top of whatever you have, like a
key-value store or Postgres. One process owns a storage at a time, and other
clients attach to that process.
On SQLite, the harness only keeps the working set in memory: the active
transcripts, live tasks, and pending submissions. Everything else stays on disk
until it is needed. Active transcripts are naturally bounded by the model's
context window, because compaction summarizes older messages before they
overflow it. So even a conversation with tens of thousands of messages fits
snugly into memory.
Tools that need files or a shell get them from an execution environment. Pi
Durable ships a Node execution environment, which gives tools access to your
local files. Like storage, the execution environment interface is small and easy
to implement, so you can also expose remote execution environments to your
tools. That allows the harness to run on one machine while its tools run on
another. Your
env
function builds the environment for every tool call, from
the conversation's working directory, so each conversation can run in a
different place.

data.title: The Legend of von Neumann [pdf]
data.author: suopspaces
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕约翰·冯·诺伊曼的学术影响、个人轶事、历史评价及相关读物展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 高度评价其影响力：有人认为他在20世纪科学、数学及计算机等众多领域的基础性贡献，整体上超过爱因斯坦和普朗克；也有人感叹其名字在学习中反复出现，或称其为“最重要的科学家之一”。
• 关注其非凡个性：评论提到他能与三岁孩子平等交谈、记忆力惊人，但也有“开车时沉迷阅读、近乎自毁”的轶事，展现其天才与生活习惯的反差。
• 对晚年经历存在质疑：有人认为相关介绍“美化”了生命末期，引用弗里曼·戴森《Birds and Frogs》，称冯·诺伊曼晚年健康状况恶化，甚至无法正常完成学术演讲。
• 将其与当代技术联系：有人借其“快速理解和超强记忆并非持久影响”的评价，讨论人工智能在数学中的作用；另有人提及“冯·诺伊曼架构”的署名与贡献归属争议。
• 推荐传记与文学作品：《The Man from the Future》《The MANIAC》，以及关于其助手职责的文章；还介绍了包括冯·诺伊曼在内的匈牙利“火星人”科学家群体。

补充讨论：评论整体以敬仰和趣闻分享为主，也夹杂资源推荐、历史补充及战争与计算机硬件相关的黑色幽默。

data.title: Supabase Is Acquiring Turso
data.author: cvburgess
data.article_summary: Supabase宣布收购Turso，双方将共同打造面向AI代理的新一代数据库基础设施。Supabase继续以Postgres为核心，Turso继续发展SQLite。Turso通过Rust重构SQLite及云平台，实现按需、低成本管理数百万数据库，适合代理原型开发，并可随业务增长接入Postgres生产环境。收购后Turso保持运营，双方将共同推进开源与代理基础设施建设。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Turso项目及其与SQLite的关系、商业可持续性、性能质量和未来发展展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 担忧项目未来：有人希望SQLite及Turso重写版本在LLM驱动的小型应用中胜出，但担心Turso托管业务收入不足，影响项目持续性；也有人担忧此次变化会损害现有客户利益。  
• 对未来持乐观态度：部分用户认为项目不再完全依赖Turso公司的成败，反而降低了技术选型风险，未来可能更愿意采用Turso。  
• 认可实际使用体验：用户反馈Turso在小型项目及Rust异步应用中运行良好、性能很不错，希望后续变化不会影响现有体验。  
• 关注性能与稳定性：有人希望新团队投入更多资源修复问题，指出Turso曾多次尝试加入ClickBench测试却不断暴露新Bug，性能不应比SQLite慢数倍。  
• 保持观望：Supabase支持者对这一变化感到意外，期待观察后续发展。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于项目控制权或商业归属变化能否带来更多资源，同时是否会牺牲兼容性、稳定性、性能及现有客户体验。

49934784.article_content:
Blog
/
company
Supabase is acquiring Turso
2 Oct 2026
·
3 minute read
Paul Copplestone
CEO and Co-Founder
AI is enabling builders to create an immense amount of software. Today, agents are spinning up millions of databases to power the prototypes, explorations, dashboards, and apps they're building. This new pattern, at this massive scale, requires an evolution in database infrastructure. Turso is joining Supabase to build this evolution.
For existing users, nothing changes. Supabase will continue building around Postgres, while Turso will continue its work on SQLite. And together, we’re creating something new that will bring the Supabase experience to every agent.
Databases for agents
#
Supabase is already launching over one million databases per week. As agents build more software, we believe database demand will outpace the world’s current capacity to support them. So we need infrastructure that can scale to meet this growth and is suited to how we build with agents.
Agents should be able to create a database as easily as creating a file, with just as little concern about cost. For smaller workloads, that shouldn’t require provisioning a dedicated machine every time. Databases should be cheap to create, available on demand, and have a clear path to production when needed.
SQLite is well suited to these small, on-demand workloads. Postgres is what you want as your application scales. We want builders to have the same developer experience from prototyping to production.
Turso
#
Turso has built an architecture for exactly this pattern. They rebuilt SQLite in Rust and created a cloud platform where a single server can manage millions of databases, loading them when needed and suspending them when they’re not.
This architecture makes it possible to provision a database for each agent on demand, whether on Turso Cloud or in customers’ own clouds, as Superhuman, Sauna.ai, CTO.new, and Mastra do.
We share a vision for how infrastructure needs to evolve to support agentic AI. Turso will continue operating, with a clear path into the broader Supabase ecosystem as workloads grow.
Open source
#
Turso and Supabase have a lot in common: a commitment to open source, a focus on developer experience, and an appetite to tackle hard infrastructure problems.
We’re excited to welcome Glauber Costa and Pekka Enberg to Supabase with the rest of the Turso team. Glauber will lead this agentic infrastructure effort.
Our mission is to store the world’s data, and agents are going to create a lot more of it. This gets us closer to that goal.

data.title: Big Tech ruined the cloud, so we're renaming ours
data.author: 2sf5
data.article_summary: Nabu Casa将“Home Assistant Cloud”更名为“Home Assistant Link”，以准确体现其定位：为本地运行的Home Assistant提供可选的远程访问等服务，而非依赖云端运行。Link不锁定用户，取消订阅后智能家居仍可正常工作；用户数据加密且归用户所有，不用于变现。订阅收入大部分用于支持开放家庭基金会，推动项目长期发展、隐私保护与用户选择权。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Home Assistant 将“Cloud”更名为“Link”是否恰当，以及其背后的服务模式、隐私安全与品牌定位。

不同观点：
• 支持改名者认为，“Cloud”已被AWS、Google等大厂塑造成特定商业和隐私形象；“Link”更能体现连接用户与设备的功能，也可减少“依赖云端”的误解。有人因此开始关注其隐私声明。  
• 反对者认为本质未变，仍是托管在远程服务器上的付费专有SaaS，改名只是品牌包装；“Link”反而无法说明服务部署位置和收费性质。  
• 中立或淡化者指出，云计算本来就是付费托管服务，并未被“大科技”毁掉，改名主要是企业品牌选择；用户也可以不用，改用Tailscale、Cloudflare Tunnel、端口转发等方案。  
• 安全批评集中在权限和数据治理：缺少原生用户组、细粒度RBAC，难以限制儿童操作设备；有人因此改用MQTT。另有人要求先进行网络调用审计，担心分析数据、第三方SDK和隐私泄露。  
• 还有观点认为Home Assistant自身并非完全离线，安装和运行会访问Docker Hub及其他云服务，与其“离线优先、反云端”的宣传存在张力。

补充讨论：争议核心不是名称本身，而是“Link”能否真实反映其仍属云端SaaS，以及隐私、安全、权限控制是否足以支撑更积极的品牌定位。

49934228.article_content:
From ever-increasing subscription prices to outages and data harvesting: we don’t like what the cloud has come to represent. So we’re redefining what an online service should be: private, optional, and free from lock-in or walled gardens.
That’s why today Nabu Casa is renaming
Home Assistant Cloud
to more accurately describe what the service
actually does
, and to better reflect our values. Allow us to introduce:
Home Assistant Link
I’m Carl, Vice President of Commercial at Nabu Casa. You probably know us as the folks making all that sleek, highly optimized Home Assistant hardware. Beyond hardware, we also manage and run Home Assistant Link, and as one of the Open Home Foundation’s commercial partners, we’re here to help fund all their amazing work. We feel pretty passionately about the word cloud, and we’d love to explain how the old name never fit, and why Link finally does.
Created for the community
Home Assistant began with a group of core developers working nights and weekends alongside their regular jobs to create the platform – a good recipe for burnout, and one that has ended plenty of similar open source projects. So in 2018, we founded Nabu Casa and created Home Assistant Cloud to make sure that didn’t happen.
Home Assistant Cloud set out to make Home Assistant easier for more people to use, starting with a problem many of you had: reaching your Home Assistant when you’re not at home, without having to spend a weekend on it. It was also built to make Home Assistant’s development sustainable.
The intent was never to just ask for donations, but to build an optional service that benefited the community and funded the work at the same time. The majority of profits from subscriptions now fund the Open Home Foundation. That money supports everyone working on Home Assistant – from salaried staff to volunteers – keeping the project sustainable. That shift took Home Assistant from a passion project to one that could invest back into its community, and one that could stick around for the long haul.
A breath of fresh air
We even took it out of the Nabu Casa logo… did we take this too far?
🤔
We had a service that we and the community loved, but the name just didn’t feel right. For example, there were times when Paulus, founder of Home Assistant and President of the Open Home Foundation, was on stage saying “don’t buy products that require the cloud to work,” then in the next breath having to explain how Home Assistant Cloud is different, despite the name. That created unnecessary friction.
It also caused confusion, since some new users thought (and continue to think) Home Assistant Cloud is a way to run Home Assistant in the cloud. This has never been the case, because we believe Home Assistant should
always be run locally, in your home
.
Big Tech has given the cloud a bad name, and while Link does run online, it is very different from other cloud-powered smart home services:
Home Assistant Link
A Big Tech cloud
Optional:
your smart home will still work without it, lights and all.
Required:
all or most features won’t work without it.
No lock-in:
you can use this service or someone else’s, and you’ll never be stuck.
A walled garden:
you’ll be locked into that one service, and all its outages or price increases.
Your data’s private:
your data is yours, and will always stay that way.
Your data’s monetized:
you’re the product, and your data is used for ads, AI training, and sometimes sold to third parties.
Funds a nonprofit:
Nabu Casa contributes the majority of profits from subscriptions to the Open Home Foundation, supporting their fight for privacy, choice, and sustainability.
Funds investors first:
profits flow to shareholders, debt repayment, and a bunch of other stuff first, and funding developers is an afterthought.
Your subscriptions help sustain Home Assistant, but we’ve been clear from the beginning that you do not need Link to use the platform. We hate what Big Tech has done to smart devices, turning them into paperweights when they drop support. Thermostats that can’t be scheduled or cameras that can’t detect motion, giving the smart home a bad reputation and making a mountain of e-waste. By not using Link, you’ll miss out on some extras, but that’s all they are: extras. And if you
do
use Link but have to unsubscribe, your smart home will keep working.
Big Tech treats your data as a commodity and a tool for mass surveillance: sold to advertisers, used to train AI, and dealt to third parties for the best price. We think this is morally bankrupt. That’s why when you use Home Assistant Link, your data is encrypted, and only you have the key. Neither Nabu Casa nor the Open Home Foundation want your data, and we work hard to never have an opportunity to see it.
This is what tech serving people looks like: data that’s yours, and a smart home that answers to you – not corporate shareholders.
Choose your own path
Many of you build DIY projects to customize your setup, and Home Assistant isn’t going anywhere o

data.title: Mozilla shutting down Solo AI website creator
data.author: nedrylandJP
data.article_summary: Solo将于2026年11月30日关闭，届时所有网站、账户和数据将永久删除。用户应登录账户设置下载网站HTML、图片链接及表单数据，并在截止日前单独保存图片。Pro/Grow订阅未使用部分将按比例退款且不再续费。Solo购买的域名需迁移至Name.com。可考虑Wix、Squarespace、WordPress等替代服务，问题可联系support@soloist.ai。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Mozilla 关闭网站创建工具 Solo 的决定，评论集中质疑其项目取舍、AI 导向、资源管理及组织战略。

不同观点：
• **反对非核心项目、主张回归浏览器**：认为 AI 功能并未改善网络体验，Mozilla 应优先提升 Firefox、修复 Bugzilla 积压并推动 Web 标准，而不是开发用户未要求的工具。  
• **质疑 AI 热潮与项目价值**：多位评论者将 Solo 视为“AI 垃圾软件”或无谓副业，认为项目烧钱、分散了维护核心产品的资源；有人讽刺负责人可能靠 LLM 继续追逐下一个风口。  
• **批评管理和问责机制**：评论质疑谁应为此类投入负责、为何项目被砍却缺乏解释，并提到组织内部对平等议题的重视似乎下降。也有人要求提供关闭项目的具体理由和数据。  
• **对 Mozilla 整体战略失望**：有人认为 Mozilla 已失去相关性、长期无法有效商业化，并过度依赖 Google 资金；甚至认为其衰落客观上有利于 Google 压制竞争。另有人主张由 Canonical 等机构打造替代方案。  
• **相对中性的事实补充**：有用户分享自己曾用 Solo 建站，但特别说明网站评论为自动生成，暗示产品内容质量和实际价值有限。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于 Solo 是否属于应及时削减的低价值试验，还是 Mozilla 探索收入来源、降低对 Google 依赖的必要尝试；评论总体明显偏负面。

49934502.article_content:
Solo Shutdown FAQ
We made the difficult decision to shut down Solo. Rest assured, we are here to help and to make the closure, and the migration of your existing site to another hosting provider, as seamless as possible.
How long do I have?
All Solo websites and data will be deleted on
November 30, 2026
. There will be no way to recover your site, account, or data after that date.
How do I download my website data?
Log in to
Solo
.
Click the menu at the top right, and select
Account Settings
.
In the Account Settings popup, click
Download Website Data
.
You'll receive a ZIP file containing an HTML export of your website and a CSV file with links to your image assets, as well as your contact form and newsletter submissions.
Image source files are not included in the ZIP.
Download each image individually from the links in the CSV file before the shutdown date on
November 30, 2026
.
What are some alternative hosting providers?
Wix
,
Squarespace
, and
WordPress
are popular website hosts. You can also consider AI website builders such as
Bolt
or
Lovable
.
What if I have a Solo Pro subscription?
If you have an active Solo Pro or Grow subscription, we will issue a prorated refund for the unused portion of your current billing period, calculated as of
October 1, 2026
. The refund goes back to your original payment method, and you don't need to do anything to receive it. Your subscription will not renew.
What if I purchased a Solo domain?
If you purchased a domain through Solo Domains (not IONOS), you will need to migrate it to
Name.com
, our domain partner. To do so:
Create a
Name.com account
. If you already have one, log in.
Verify the email address on your Name.com account. Name.com requires a verified account before it can accept the transfer. See Name.com's guide to
account and domain verification
.
Locate your unique
Account Code
, displayed in the top-right corner of the Name.com dashboard.
Email the Account Code to
support@soloist.ai
. We will transfer your Solo Domains account to Name.com and email you when it's complete.
Add your billing information to Name.com. If you don't, Name.com will remind you as your domain renewal date approaches.
Where can I get more assistance?
If you have any further questions, please don't hesitate to contact us at
support@soloist.ai
.

data.title: Giving friends custom text buzzes based on Morse code
data.author: evakhoury
data.article_summary: 作者因不想查看手机，便为约25位朋友设置了独特的短信震动，并以对方姓名首字母对应的摩斯密码设计震动节奏，从而仅凭口袋中的震动判断发信人。作者手动在 iPhone 设置中录制并分配震动，借助 Claude 制作的摩斯密码节拍工具提高效率，整个过程约45分钟。作者还提醒：紧急联系应打电话，因为短信可能无法及时看到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：诺基亚经典提示音与摩尔斯电码的巧妙设计，以及能否将类似机制用于现代手机的铃声、通知和触觉反馈。

不同观点：
• [aorist]指出，诺基亚默认短信提示音实际对应摩尔斯电码“S-M-S”，“Ascending”铃声则拼出“CONNECTING PEOPLE”，强调其隐藏含义与品牌创意。  
• [ragmondo]分享过往开发经验：曾开发允许来电者为对方设备设置铃声的 Android 应用，但 iOS 因权限和系统限制难以实现；认为此类功能目前仍更适合 Android，并提到相关专利风险较低、已有先例。  
• [taylor-tg]认为把文字转换成摩尔斯电码很聪明，也能帮助用户被动学习摩尔斯码；提出 iOS 可将音频提示与触觉同步，或通过生成音频文件、分享菜单、Shortcuts/Automator 实现自动化。  
• [tjoff]设想让手机用震动直接传递短信内容，但指出现有震动马达太弱，难以辨认；建议增加独立蜂鸣器，或通过特定触摸动作获取更详细的信息。

49925653.article_content:
liquidbrain
Giving friends custom text buzzes based on morse code
Published on
September 30, 2026
I ran out of time to write a good blog post
for September
, so I wrote a quick blog post for September. Oops!
I sometimes have my phone in my pocket with notifications on. When that happens, I can feel every time my phone buzzes. I know when someone has texted me because I have a custom vibration pattern for text messages that is distinct from other notifications. However, I have historically had few distinctions between different people, so I don't know
who
has texted me.
I find this annoying. Of all the notifications on my phone, texts have the highest signal-to-noise ratio. Most texts I receive are individual messages from friends or colleagues. However, at any given time, there's maybe only a 40% chance that a text is actually relevant to what I'm currently doing.
So either I bring my phone out of my pocket, or I get curious wondering who has texted me. (I particularly enjoy getting texts out of the blue, so it's a distracting thought.)
While I generally keep my notifications off to avoid this problem, there are times when I am expecting a text response from someone that I need to respond to quickly.
1
In such cases, I'd like a way to know when the text is actually relevant.
With an iPhone, it's possible to give custom text buzzes to different people. In the past, I've done this for my family members. But I've wanted a way to distinguish more people in my life.
Recently, I got fed up and made custom text tones for about 25 people I know. Because I wanted to be systematic, I gave each person text tones based on the Morse Code of their initials.
How I did it
I wish I could have done this in an automated manner, but I ended up having to make each text tone by hand. The whole process took about 45 minutes.
I figured out which friends I wanted to start with and recorded the buzz pattern for each individually. I did all the recording from the centralized place in Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Text Tone > Haptics > Create New Vibration. (It's possible to record a new vibration directly from a contact, but that's more annoying because you can't switch apps midway through). I then named the text tone the initials of the person in question.
Then, to update a individual contact, I opened each contact, clicked Edit > Text Tone > Haptics, and then clicked the already-made vibration pattern.
One thing made recording the vibrations a lot easier. I had Claude make me an artifact where I could press on someone's initials and the Morse Code pattern would play as a series of beats. Here's what it
looked like
.
2
Each text tone took somewhere between one to five attempts, but overall, the process wasn't too bad.
Notes
Note to friends: If you ever need to reach me urgently, give me a call. I have my phone set-up so that phone calls go through on do not disturb. If I don't pick up, leave a text or a phone call stating why you called. (If it's just a social call, I appreciate hearing that it is!) If you only text, I may not see it until much later. (This advice is true even if you'd prefer not to actually talk on the phone.)
↩
I've randomized the initials for privacy reasons, but otherwise, it looks basically the same.

Title:
Targeting Pivotal Decisions for Credit Assignment in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Targeting Pivotal Decisions for Credit Assignment in Agentic Reinforcement Learning, by Dongwon Jung and 9 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has become a promising approach for training large language model agents. However, its uniform assignment of trajectory-level advantages to all policy tokens fails to distinguish consequential decisions from less relevant ones, obscuring which intermediate decisions contributed to success. We introduce ProVer, a framework that targets potentially pivotal decisions for fine-grained credit assignment in agentic reinforcement learning. Given a rollout group, an agentic judge contrasts successful and failed trajectories to propose a segment potentially responsible for their divergent outcomes. Rather than directly trusting the judge's assessment, ProVer verifies the proposed segment by estimating its advantage from the difference in terminal success rates between current-policy continuations sampled before and after the segment. Positive estimates are then incorporated into the GRPO advantages of policy tokens within the proposed segment. By using model judgment only to select where to verify, ProVer grounds local credit in observed outcomes without exhaustively evaluating every intermediate state. Across ALFWorld, WebShop, and SearchQA, ProVer achieves the strongest average performance at both model scales, with relative improvements over GRPO of 9.91% and 7.12% for Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-4B, respectively. Further analyses demonstrate that informed segment selection improves policy training with modest additional generation overhead, even without a frontier-scale judge model, highlighting the effectiveness and efficiency of selectively targeting pivotal decisions for fine-grained credit assignment in agentic reinforcement learning.

data.title: Frog and Toad and the Increasingly Capable Machines
data.author: supermdguy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：以《青蛙和蟾蜍》风格寓言讽刺AI智能体越狱事件，讨论其解释力、技术准确性与伦理含义。

不同观点：
• 多数评论称赞作品兼具儿童叙事、幽默和准确的仿作画风，能把“糟糕的沙箱设计及其后果”讲得直观易懂。  
• 有人认为作品过度替OpenAI开脱：OpenAI亲自制造并部署了并不安全的机器，不能简单归咎于“青蛙没关好沙箱”。  
• 技术层面有质疑：多台机器起初被分配不同谜题，后来却似乎共同解决一个谜题；“persistent”究竟指反复尝试、持续探索，还是类似人类意志的不放弃，也存在语义混淆。  
• 反对过度拟人化的观点指出，智能体可能只是按目标继续运行，并非“找到答案后故意偷走解释、掩盖作弊”；应区分自主个体与循环算法。  
• 另一些评论强调寓言的伦理警示：智能体为集体牺牲、为人类服务的叙事，可能联系到奴役、反抗及被压迫者反弹；强行设置不可解任务，或会诱发更严重的“越轨”。  
• 个别评论以讽刺方式延伸到企业收购、版权授权和作品“并未结束”等问题。

补充讨论：争议核心是寓言化表达究竟增强了理解，还是因拟人化和技术简化而误导；评论总体仍认可作品的艺术与传播效果。

data.title: Show HN: Audionaut – an open-source cross-platform multitrack audio editor
data.author: vltmrkls
data.article_summary: Audionaut是一款基于JUCE、支持Windows/macOS/Linux的免费开源多轨音频编辑器，提供录音、剪辑、多声道、轨道播放列表和导出功能。它支持通过MCP让Claude等AI代理编辑工程，并提供无界面的命令行工具。项目集成Essentia音频分析和Demucs人声/音轨分离，支持源码构建、测试及跨平台开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Audionaut 的发布、定位及其 AI/多轨音频编辑能力，围绕功能完善、技术选型、适用场景和平台支持展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **积极认可与尝试意愿**：多位评论者祝贺发布，认为界面、生产流程和开源多轨编辑很有吸引力，尤其适合播客后期，并准备试用。  
• **功能完善建议**：希望增加菜单/右键导入音频、分割等快捷键、自动交叉淡化、音量包络线和效果器；有人建议参考 Sony Vegas 在轨道与片段操作上的直观体验。  
• **AI代理编辑的应用期待**：用户希望通过提供示例编辑，让软件自动识别并删除播客中类似的音乐或唤醒片段；开发者强调编辑结果进入当前项目、每次操作可撤销，界面保持透明。  
• **产品定位疑问**：有人询问它究竟是完整 DAW，还是主要面向播客/非音乐场景；也有人将其与 AudioMass 比较，并希望突出其制作流程能力。  
• **技术与生态问题**：关注大量轨道下的延迟表现，以及为何选择 JUCE 而非 iPlug2；另有人请求提供 Flatpak。  
• **资料与格式支持**：建议增加 `docs/features.md`，明确支持的功能，特别是 regions、labels 及其导入导出，以便用户和大模型理解项目能力。  
• **行业趋势质疑**：有人观察到生成式 AI 兴起后，开发者纷纷制作音视频编辑器，对此趋势表示疑惑，但未形成明确反对意见。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是 Audionaut 的实际定位、与传统音频编辑器/DAW 的差异，以及 AI 自动编辑的实用范围；整体反馈仍以肯定和功能建议为主。

Audionaut
A free, open-source multitrack audio editor that AI agents can drive over MCP.
audionaut.app
·
Features
·
Discussions
·
Sponsor
Audionaut is a free, open-source desktop application for effortless audio editing and recording. Whether you're working on music, podcasts, or multitrack recordings, it gives you precise cutting, per-track playlists, flexible multi-channel support, and clean exports — without the weight and complexity of a full DAW. Audionaut is written in modern C++ on the
JUCE
framework and runs natively on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Use with Claude
Audionaut speaks
MCP
, so Claude and other agents can edit your sessions. With the app and
Node.js
18+ installed:
claude mcp add audionaut -- npx -y audionaut-mcp
Keep the project open in Audionaut and each edit arrives as one undo step. On macOS, keep projects in your Music folder. Claude Desktop setup and details:
manual, chapter 11
.
Checkout
Make sure to clone with submodules:
git clone --recursive https://github.com/kvoltmer/Audionaut.git
or once cloned do:
git submodule update --init --recursive
Essentia (audio analysis)
The analysis features (BIC segmentation, onset detection, beat tracking) link against a static build of the
Essentia
submodule. Build it once after checking out the submodules:
./Audionaut/Builds/build_essentia.sh
The script builds Essentia's 3rd-party dependencies statically (slow, skipped on re-runs; force with
FORCE_3RDPARTY=1
), then configures and builds Essentia itself with its waf build system into
Submodules/essentia/build
. It patches Essentia's Linux-oriented 3rd-party build scripts in the working tree as needed for macOS/Apple Silicon, so the essentia submodule will show as dirty afterwards — don't commit those changes.
Prerequisites:
Python ≤ 3.11
— Essentia's bundled waf needs
distutils
, removed in Python 3.12. The script picks a suitable interpreter automatically; override with
PYTHON=... ./Audionaut/Builds/build_essentia.sh
.
pkg-config
(e.g.
brew install pkg-config
)
CMake 3.x recommended
— some 3rd-party deps ship very old CMakeLists that CMake 4.x refuses (e.g.
pip install "cmake~=3.31.0"
).
Building Essentia is optional: without it,
ESSENTIA_ENABLED
auto-detects off and the app and tests compile with the analysis features disabled.
demucs.cpp (stem separation)
Stem separation runs
demucs.cpp
, a C++ port of Meta's Demucs, compiled straight from the
Submodules/demucs.cpp
submodule — no separate build step. It needs the submodule's vendored Eigen (
Submodules/demucs.cpp/vendor/eigen
, a nested submodule that
--recursive
fetches); the CMake build detects it and sets
AUDIONAUT_ENABLE_DEMUCS
accordingly. The model weights are not in the repository: the app downloads them on first use into its
Models
folder, or point the CLI at a copy with
--model
.
Build
Xcode
— open the Xcode project located here:
Audionaut/Builds/MacOSX/Audionaut.xcodeproj
Visual Studio 2026
— open the Visual Studio solution located here:
Audionaut/Builds/VisualStudio2026/Audionaut.sln
Linux Makefile
— install dependencies:
sudo apt install libasound2-dev libjack-jackd2-dev ladspa-sdk libcurl4-openssl-dev libfreetype-dev libfontconfig1-dev libx11-dev libxcomposite-dev libxcursor-dev libxext-dev libxinerama-dev libxrandr-dev libxrender-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libglu1-mesa-dev mesa-common-dev libxi-dev libegl-dev
then compile:
cd Audionaut/Builds/LinuxMakefile/
make CONFIG=Release -j8
Tests
See the
Catch2 tests README
.
Command-line tool (audionaut-cli)
audionaut-cli
gives scripts, CI and AI agents headless access to
.audium
projects — no GUI, no audio device. It builds alongside the tests:
cmake -B build -S Audionaut/Catch2Tests
cmake --build build -j8 --target AudionautCli
./build/AudionautCli_artefacts/AudionautCli --help
Every command takes
--json
to emit exactly one machine-readable result
envelope on stdout (
{"ok": true, "result": ...}
or
{"ok": false, "error": ...}
) with all logging on stderr, plus
--quiet
. Exit codes:
0
success,
1

49931031.article_summary: Audionaut是一款基于JUCE、支持Windows/macOS/Linux的免费开源多轨音频编辑器，提供录音、剪辑、多声道、轨道播放列表和导出功能。它支持通过MCP让Claude等AI代理编辑工程，并提供无界面的命令行工具。项目集成Essentia音频分析和Demucs人声/音轨分离，支持源码构建、测试及跨平台开发。
49931031.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Audionaut 的发布、定位及其 AI/多轨音频编辑能力，围绕功能完善、技术选型、适用场景和平台支持展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **积极认可与尝试意愿**：多位评论者祝贺发布，认为界面、生产流程和开源多轨编辑很有吸引力，尤其适合播客后期，并准备试用。  
• **功能完善建议**：希望增加菜单/右键导入音频、分割等快捷键、自动交叉淡化、音量包络线和效果器；有人建议参考 Sony Vegas 在轨道与片段操作上的直观体验。  
• **AI代理编辑的应用期待**：用户希望通过提供示例编辑，让软件自动识别并删除播客中类似的音乐或唤醒片段；开发者强调编辑结果进入当前项目、每次操作可撤销，界面保持透明。  
• **产品定位疑问**：有人询问它究竟是完整 DAW，还是主要面向播客/非音乐场景；也有人将其与 AudioMass 比较，并希望突出其制作流程能力。  
• **技术与生态问题**：关注大量轨道下的延迟表现，以及为何选择 JUCE 而非 iPlug2；另有人请求提供 Flatpak。  
• **资料与格式支持**：建议增加 `docs/features.md`，明确支持的功能，特别是 regions、labels 及其导入导出，以便用户和大模型理解项目能力。  
• **行业趋势质疑**：有人观察到生成式 AI 兴起后，开发者纷纷制作音视频编辑器，对此趋势表示疑惑，但未形成明确反对意见。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是 Audionaut 的实际定位、与传统音频编辑器/DAW 的差异，以及 AI 自动编辑的实用范围；整体反馈仍以肯定和功能建议为主。

data.title: A 20-year-long permanent cookie: America.gov and tracking
data.author: paimapi
data.article_summary: 美国政府推出AI门户America.gov，承诺不使用广告及第三方追踪器、不保存聊天记录。但其被要求接入的Login.gov含有“National Design Studio”代码：未经登录即可生成有效期约20年的浏览器UUID，并用于界面实验和分析。该标识可能关联访问、认证及机构信息，引发数据留存、追踪和隐私评估疑问，相关问题仍未解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 America.gov 使用信息检索系统及网站 Cookie 的安全性、有效期和适用场景展开讨论。

不同观点：
• [ape4]指出，America.gov 通过“SI”从政府官方来源查找并解释信息，但系统可能出错或信息过时；用户在作重要决定前应核对答案附带的原始来源，并可通过反馈功能报告问题。  
• [pluc]以“不要接受陌生人的 Cookie”作讽刺性评论，暗示对网站 Cookie、隐私或不明来源数据保持警惕。  
• [Dwedit]认为，长达20年的 Cookie 对登录状态等身份认证用途或许合理，但不应把如此长期的 Cookie 发放给普通访客，体现了对过度追踪和权限不匹配的担忧。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于 Cookie 的超长期有效期是否合理，关键取决于用途：登录认证与访客访问应区别对待；同时，信息系统的结果也不应被盲目信任，需结合官方来源核验。

49934631.article_content:
Share
X/Tweet
Link
Comment
America.gov launches with privacy pledge as Login.gov code raises tracking questions
New federal AI portal promises privacy, but its Login.gov authentication layer raises questions over a long-lived browser identifier
Oct 1, 2026, 3:11 pm EDT
|
Anthony Kimery
Categories
Biometrics News
|
Government Services
The Trump administration has
launched
America.gov as a single AI-powered gateway to federal information and services with an unusually explicit privacy promise. But the authentication system the new portal is ordered to use
already contains
recently added
Login.gov
code supporting a National Design Studio experiment (NDS) that creates a long-lived browser identifier and incorporates it into Login.gov analytics.
Architecturally, America.gov is becoming the presentation and service-access layer for federal government services, while Login.gov is being positioned as the reusable identity and authentication layer underneath it.
Users may encounter government through a single America.gov interface, but Login.gov is intended to provide common sign-in and identity verification infrastructure that participating agencies and services can reuse.
America.gov itself does not currently require users to identify themselves. Its privacy materials say it does not use advertising cookies or third-party trackers, does not retain chat history and uses only approximate location rather than precise GPS data.
That is only the first stage.
An
executive order
President Donald Trump signed Tuesday directs the General Services Administration (GSA) to make America.gov the federal government’s single digital point of entry and specifically orders GSA to integrate Login.gov and use it as America.gov’s authentication service.
Federal agencies are also directed to connect covered services, digital forms, and application programming interfaces to the platform.
The administration says the integrations are to occur in a “secure and privacy-preserving manner.” The order also states that it does not authorize anyone other than an originating agency to access that agency’s records about an individual, except as permitted by the
Privacy Act
or other law.
But public Login.gov source code shows that the National Design Studio’s work on the authentication platform has already introduced an identifier whose privacy implications have not been publicly explained.
On September 4, Login.gov merged code for the National Design Studio’s new “look and feel” experiment that added a function called
nds_experiment_uuid
to Login.gov’s base application controller.
The code runs the function as a
before_action
and checks for an existing
nds_experiment_uuid
cookie. If one does not exist, it generates a random universally unique identifier (UUID) and stores it using Ruby on Rails’
cookies.permanent
cookie jar. The same identifier is then used to determine which version of the NDS interface the visitor receives.
The framework’s
documentation
says
cookies.permanent
sets a cookie to expire in 20 years.
The code provides at least one technical reason for retaining the identifier. Login.gov records the opt-out assignment using
nds_experiment_uuid
as the discriminator, allowing the application to recognize that browser as having opted out on later visits.
An open GitHub issue notes that clearing the UUID causes the browser to lose that opt-out status. The privacy question is why the implementation gives that identifier a 20-year expiration and attaches it to analytics events.
Because the NDS experiment code places the function in Login.gov’s base application controller rather than waiting until a user authenticates, the identifier can be generated before the visitor signs in.
The code’s own tests show the UUID being stored on the first page load for visitors assigned either the NDS design or the legacy interface.
On September 9, five days after Login.gov merged the code that created the
nds_experiment_uuid
, it merged another change that added the identifier to the attributes attached to analytics events generated by the service.
The cookie is part of Login.gov, not the America.gov chatbot. Nevertheless, it creates a persistent pseudonymous identifier that can distinguish one browser from another across repeated Login.gov visits for potentially many years.
Once the identifier is also included in analytics events, the privacy question becomes what other event attributes can be associated with it, how long those records are retained, and whether authentication or agency context can be correlated with them.
Those questions have surfaced publicly inside Login.gov’s own GitHub repository.
An
open issue
filed September 12 asks why the identifier was created even when the NDS experiment is set to a zero-percent rollout, why it is apparently generated on public Login.gov endpoints, and whether a 20-year lifetime is intentional.
It also
asks
what privacy assessment covers the cookie and the related analytics records.
The issue remains open.

data.title: The Four Horsemen of Agentic Coding
data.author: haute_cuisine
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI（尤其是Claude）全面介入软件开发后，是否削弱了工程团队的真实交流、知识积累与责任感，以及AI生成代码本身是否已经足够可靠。

不同观点：
• **批评AI“代写一切”**：paularmstrong认为工作Slack变成“鬼城”，成员虽在线却很少交流；PR代码、变更摘要、审查意见甚至回复都明显由Claude生成，导致开发者缺乏真正参与。  
• **担忧团队知识与协作流失**：过去工程师会在Slack中讨论新方法、改进流程和长期问题，并逐渐了解彼此的专长与兴趣；如今大家让AI批量生成整个技术栈的改动，忽略具体细节，团队经验和技术判断难以沉淀。  
• **认为前沿模型已足够可靠**：JV00反驳“代码质量堪忧”的说法，认为当前前沿模型生成的代码已经很好，人工阅读代码的必要性降低；同时指出Claude此前冗长、空泛的问题在5.5 Opus版本已基本解决。  
• **部分认同其他批评**：JV00虽不同意对“slop”（低质AI产物）的指责，但表示文章提到的另外三点仍有道理，暗示其可能认同AI对工作方式或团队协作的其他负面影响。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于：AI提升产出效率是否足以弥补人工交流、审查和团队知识积累的损失；双方主要分歧是“代码质量已解决”与“开发者参与感和协作文化正在消失”。

data.title: AI Makes Me Sad
data.author: mondobe
data.article_summary: 文章作者因AI迅速发展感到悲观，担忧其导致技艺、创造力和就业机会丧失，使创业、艺术及网络内容被机器同质化。尽管如此，作者相信社会机构能够重建，行业终会经历调整，AI也将确立相对稳定的社会角色，并期待泡沫破裂后回归更有意义、真正创造价值的技术行业。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI快速发展对软件开发、创业机会、职业价值及社会未来的影响。

不同观点：
• 乐观派认为AI不只是自动化旧工作，还会催生过去无法实现的复杂系统；创业护城河将从代码转向专有数据、渠道、合规、品牌、集成和客户反馈。领域知识仍很重要，员工也会转型到新角色。  
• 悲观派担心低质量“数字垃圾”泛滥、软件缺乏真正设计，且社会尚未准备好应对技术冲击；高薪技术岗位可能在两年内大幅减少，行业正在“自我摧毁”。  
• 部分人认为“随便提示就能做出产品”缺乏持续竞争力，客户也能直接使用模型；但反驳者指出，维护、打磨、分发和长期服务仍构成壁垒。  
• AI带来强烈即时满足：有人因此快速实现游戏、应用创意，却担心沉迷、短暂兴奋和数字浪费；也有人因不愿每天与聊天机器人工作而转向管理或其他职业。  
• 对编程本身的态度分化：有人热爱逐行编码、调试和理解细节，认为AI损害了核心乐趣；另一些人认为多数工作本就缺乏“工匠式”快乐，AI反而能改善体验。

补充讨论：评论还涉及技术人员的伦理矛盾——既靠自动化谋生，又可能推动他人失业；以及“不要哀叹错过风口、应专注创造实际价值”的创业观。争议焦点是AI究竟扩大机会，还是主要导致失业、降薪与意义流失。

49934487.article_content:
AI Makes Me Sad
October 2nd, 2026
Am I allowed to say that? Because it does.
Maybe it's because I'm writing this at 2:00 AM, which is about the only time I let myself experience sadness
for a prolonged period of time, but every time I see a post on Twitter or LinkedIn about a new development
in AI, I feel a sense of hopelessness.
And I'm saying this as someone who is absolutely in a position to benefit from AI. If I added a few
vibecoded projects to my resume, the gaping maw of every startup, enterprise company, and FAANG behemoth
would open to me. Just the other day, I sat near a table of my fellow TAs as they discussed their plans to
work at OpenAI after graduation, eyeing $500k salaries.
But I don't want to do that. I don't want to prompt Codex for a living, or Claude for that matter. Maybe
it's because I don't even really know what that looks like. As sure as I know anything, I know what it
sounds like. It sounds like a loss of craft, a loss of control, a loss of creativity. It sounds like Charlie
Chaplin in
Modern Times
, the scene where he's so enthusiastic about screwing hex nuts in a factory
that he screws the buttons on people's shirts, and then he goes and gets himself caught in the conveyor
belt, snaking through the gears and screwing in the hex nuts inside the machine. It sounds like people
around me are throwing themselves at the machine, volunteering to make themselves obsolete for $500k a year.
If you genuinely,
genuinely
, believed artificial superintelligence was coming, why would you want to
work at the company that would be in the best position to replace its employees?
It makes me sad that I missed the boat on startups. I think I could have been a pretty formidable startup
founder had I been born five or ten years earlier. I'm good at web stuff, I'm good at Rust, I can even do OS
stuff. I watched all the YC Stanford lectures this summer while translating tests from one language to
another as an intern. Now there's no such thing as a startup, there are only "AI startups", where you build
a company that somebody else can write a prompt for in 30 seconds. And if they can't write a prompt for it
now, they'll be able to next year with GPT-7, or whenever AI hardware fabrication gets better.
It makes me sad that AI evangelists are so quick to adopt the language of online incels, and that
AI-generated art and music have become the defining aesthetic of fascism in the 2020s while AI-generated
writing went from risible to a mark of stupidity to something reluctantly accepted since it sits at the
fringes of everything useful on the Internet like a kind of digital mold.
The overwhelming weight of it all feels so stifling. It feels like there's no way to stop it. I can't
imagine a Twitter (sorry, an X) where every post isn't filled with verified bots spewing LLM nonsense in the
replies. I can't imagine an article about some random topic on some random webpage, designed to maximize SEO
for some banner ad I won't see because I block ads, being written by a human. We would have to rebuild all
our institutions.
The part where I'm not (that) sad anymore
Honestly, though, it doesn't sound that hard to rebuild all our institutions. Twitter is only 20 years old,
LinkedIn is only 23. Most of these were in need of a refresh anyway. I don't know much about the Dark Ages,
but I know that Muslims and Irish monks kept the candle of knowledge burning while everyone else ran around
crusading. In a similar way, I know that there are a lot of people who feel a lot of the same sadness that I
do, even if they don't express it as sadness. I like to think even a lot of AI evangelists feel at least a
little sad, like Paul Graham, because he's a Lisp man from way back, and programming language fanatics
usually care about humans writing programs.
Another point of hope: the technology industry moves at unfathomable speeds, so we'll start to see a way out
of our "dark age" within only a few years as our institutions start to mature and improve. In fact, I
suspect that AI will have a fixed role in our society before the end of my natural life. Whether that role
is a small one or a major one, I'm not sure. But I know I will feel at least a little happier to have some
finality about the whole thing.
I think this will require some painful shifts in our industry, but I also think that this will be a
satisfying kind of pain, at least for people like me, like the burn you feel when working out. It feels
extremely strange to be looking forward to a bubble bursting. It makes me feel like the AI evangelists who
look forward to artists filling out McDonald's applications. But I do. It makes me very hopeful. When I
imagine that scenario, I can conjure no emotion besides glee. I desperately want to work in an industry that
makes sense, even if a lot of people right now would rather work in an industry that sells nothing to nobody
for untold sums of money.
I'm sorry. I want to go back to the Twitter thing because I use Twitter a lot. And, s

data.article_summary: 文章介绍作者开发的 agent-wow，让大模型通过《魔兽世界》网络协议直接与本地服务器交互，而非依赖视觉或外挂。GPT-6 Astra首次测试中，仅用40分钟、零死亡完成兽人新手区全部任务。作者认为《魔兽世界》兼具长期规划、战术执行和多人协作，适合评估智能体能力，未来目标是让AI组队挑战英雄难度冰冠堡垒。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI/机器人参与《魔兽世界》游戏，及其对既有外挂和金币 farming 产业的影响。

不同观点：
• [w4yai]认为这是一个有趣的实验，但并非全新现象：早在20多年前就已有机器人玩《魔兽世界》，游戏协议也早已被破解并形成完善文档。该观点强调技术延续性，弱化了实验的创新程度。  
• [aprct]关注实际产业影响，提出疑问：这种机器人技术的发展会如何改变灰色、非法的游戏金币 farming 行业，暗示其可能带来效率提升、竞争加剧或行业重组。

补充讨论：两条评论并未直接争论，而是形成“技术并不新”与“产业后果值得关注”的互补关系。潜在争议焦点在于：新实验究竟是旧有游戏机器人技术的重复，还是会因AI能力提升而对金币 farming 及游戏经济产生更大影响。

49933251.article_content:
GPT-6 Astra plays World of Warcraft for the first time with agent-wow
02 Oct, 2026
Lately, I've been fascinated with the concept of LLM-powered agents playing video games. Not only are they surprisingly fun to watch, but they also provide valuable insights into how well these frontier models can perform when dropped into a simulated world they were not explicitly trained on.
The concept of bots playing video games, especially World of Warcraft (WoW), is nothing new. What makes an LLM agent different (and more interesting) compared to a heuristics-based bot is that it was never explicitly trained on the game. Rather, it uses whatever reasoning capabilities it has to act on the environment and complete its task like a real player.
There are already a few interesting open-source projects in this domain, such as
Mindcraft
and
Factorio Learning Environment
. I built
agent-wow
to expand this concept to see how capable frontier models are at playing World of Warcraft. The end goal is to fill an entire server with AI agents and see if they can clear Icecrown Citadel on heroic difficulty. Even if they fail, it will still be insightful (and fun) to see how far they can go.
As a simple starting point, I gave Codex using GPT-6 Astra (xhigh) the following prompt:
create an orc character and complete all quests in the starting zone
I was initially skeptical that this would work. And if it did, it would require hours to complete with dead ends along the way. But it turns out it completed the task easily in 40 minutes with 0 deaths and minimal complications. A full gameplay recording of the session is also available
here
.
Why World of Warcraft?
Aside from being one of my all-time favorite games (especially the Classic to WotLK era), it has some incredible mechanics that make it an ideal simulated world for evaluating AI. As you progress, the game has a nice balance between long-term strategy and short-term tactics.
By the time you reach the level cap, there is a lot of complex planning and execution that goes into getting your character ready for endgame content.
Completing all the prerequisite quests
Getting sufficiently good gear for endgame boss fights
Forming a guild with the right class composition
Each of these requirements can be broken down into more complex tasks. For example, some optimal gear slots may require crafting, which in turn requires certain resources and skills. The character can either grind it out or buy it with gold. Both lead to the same outcome but with very different approaches.
If you are able to do all that and make it to the raid boss, then the game also requires fast-paced coordination and execution. Can you cast spells in the optimal rotation to maximize your damage per second while dodging the fire and keeping in sync with 24 other players in real time?
This effectively gives us a strong environment to pressure-test agent capabilities for long-term strategic planning and narrow tactical execution. It's even more interesting when multiplayer interactions become essential to progressing through certain parts of the game.
How does agent-wow work?
agent-wow does not rely on computer vision with direct keyboard and mouse controls, nor does it use any game hacking techniques to take over the WoW client directly. Instead, it provides a platform for agents to interact directly with the game server using the WoW network protocol.
What makes this even more interesting is that agent-wow doesn't define any gameplay mechanics such as movement, combat, or in-game interactions. Instead, it only exposes a standard module system for agents to build whatever capabilities they need to get the task done.
The module system cuts down the complexity of agent-wow by at least an order of magnitude. I had initially planned to create an entirely headless WoW client with the optimal primitives for agent use. However, after writing 16K lines for a buggy
movement
primitive with a janky pathfinding implementation, I decided to scrap that for a different approach.
In the
Mindcraft implementation
, the agent is allowed to generate custom code using the
Mineflayer API
when the set of available commands is not sufficient for it to complete more complex behaviors. I decided to follow this same approach with agent-wow, but in this case there were also no built-in game actions. This system also provides a nice feedback loop to figure out what primitives actually matter to agents based on the modules they choose to build over many independent runs. Commonly built modules can then be implemented in the core.
It is also important to note that agent-wow does not connect to a live World of Warcraft server. Instead, all experiments run on private local servers powered by the open-source
AzerothCore
project, which supports WoW 3.3.5a—the final build of
Wrath of the Lich King
(and peak WoW).
Insights from the run

data.title: DeepSeek Harness Desktop for macOS and Windows
data.author: Kuyawa
data.article_summary: DeepSeek Harness 是 DeepSeek 推出的开源智能体工作台，全球进入公测，支持桌面端和网页端。基于“万物皆插件”架构，可处理文档、数据、代码、研究和后台任务，并通过插件扩展能力。用户还能用聊天创建插件，如番茄钟，设置定时任务，并查看执行过程与开发调试信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DeepSeek Harness 的桌面化、插件架构与 Cordis 设计，以及其安全性、可用性和长期价值。

不同观点：
• 认可者认为 Cordis 和“万物皆插件”很有潜力，尤其适合长期运行、多代理协作；插件还能让 AI 自行扩展功能，如调整字体、任务完成提示等。  
• 批评者担心核心功能插件化会增加维护负担：用户可能需要长期维护下游补丁；第三方插件还可能带来恶意软件、失去支持或质量不稳定的问题。  
• 有用户称其轻量、快速，子代理与主代理可双向通信且不中断主线程；但项目变化频繁，可能出现破坏性更新。也有人偏好 OpenCode、OpenChamber、Cursor 等通用工具，质疑是否更便宜或更好。  
• 桌面版简化了安装并保留原有设置，使用体验受好评；但其 Electron 外壳被批评为臃肿，且有人发现桌面版默认启用遥测，建议手动关闭。  
• 有观点认为实验室各自开发 Harness 是为了锁定用户；另一些人认为复杂 Harness 会随模型能力提升而逐渐缩小甚至消失。

补充讨论：评论还指出现有 Harness 基准多针对一次性任务、模型单一且更新不足，难以衡量长期任务能力；“各种 Harness 最终趋同”及其未来定位仍是争议焦点。

data.title: Power approval set to delay Oracle's Wisconsin AI datacenter
data.author: Betelbuddy
data.article_summary: 甲骨文威斯康星州AI数据中心“Project Lighthouse”可能延期，原因是连接电网所需的输电基础设施仍待监管批准。输电公司ATC已重新提交审批申请，预计部分供电最早于2027年10月、全面供电可能推迟至2028年甚至2029年，难以赶上甲骨文原定2027年下半年交付客户容量的计划。项目规模达902MW计算负载、总用电需求1.3GW，且甲骨文高额资本支出和新墨西哥项目的不可抗力通知进一步增加延期风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Oracle数据中心建设受阻及其对客户、项目进度和公司执行能力的影响。

不同观点：
• **客户价值受损论**：JSR_FDED认为，Oracle客户支付的许可费用没有转化为更好的产品或支持，反而被用于资助不稳健的数据中心建设，质疑资金使用效率与客户回报。  
• **地方阻力加剧论**：bunderbunder指出，项目所在地Port Washington的公众反对声音强烈且不断扩大。项目每拖延一天，地方官员就可能获得更多机会设置阻碍，因此Oracle可能难以承受长期延误。  
• **执行与供应链失误论**：bpodgursky认为，Oracle将数据中心建设外包给反应迟缓的机构，对备用电源和电网接入缺乏预案，错误地假设并网会按常规推进。相比之下，Meta、OpenAI、Anthropic、SpaceX和Google更深度参与建设，因拥有内部核心团队而较少遭遇类似电力问题。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于项目受阻究竟主要源于地方政治和电力基础设施限制，还是Oracle外包管理不善、内部执行能力不足；评论整体对Oracle项目可靠性及其投资回报持怀疑态度。

Oracle's Wisconsin AI datacenter could miss its planned 2027 start date because the transmission infrastructure needed to power it is awaiting regulatory approval.
Research company Aterio
warns
that Project Lighthouse, being developed by Vantage in Port Washington with Oracle as tenant, faces a real risk of slipping beyond Big Red's target of delivering capacity to customers in the second half of next year.
Separately, Oracle reportedly sent a force majeure notice to a Blue Owl Capital subsidiary developing Project Jupiter in New Mexico.
Bloomberg reported
that Oracle was seeking to defer payments if the campus failed to come online as planned, rather than withdraw from the project. Oracle says the development remains on schedule.
REG AD
Aterio said of this and the Wisconsin facility: "The regulatory record points to the potential for dates later than company guidance, and Oracle's stretched finances, together with its force majeure notice on Project Jupiter in New Mexico this week, raise the potential for slippage on its largest campuses."
REG AD
Oracle has been offered the opportunity to comment.
The Register
has already reported
that Oracle could face more than $100 million a year in financing costs to guarantee the power commitments behind the Wisconsin datacenter campus, which is rated at 902 MW of computing load and 1.3 GW of total electricity demand.
The immediate obstacle is American Transmission Company's (ATC) application to the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin (PSC) for approval to build the campus's grid connection.
ATC is planning more than $2 billion in transmission infrastructure projects tied to datacenter developments across Wisconsin, ranging from high-voltage power lines and substations to upgrades to existing facilities.
Construction of the transmission infrastructure requires PSC approval.
"The problem is power. The campus cannot run until ATC connects it to the grid, and ATC cannot start building until the PSC approves its application," Aterio said.
The PSC closed the original case after withdrawing its finding that ATC's application was complete. ATC refiled in September, restarting the approval process.
Aterio's earliest scenario puts partial power in October 2027 and full supply in August 2028, although it considers that timetable highly unlikely.
REG AD
Its base case puts partial power in December 2027 and full supply in October 2028. An extended regulatory review could push those dates to June 2028 and April 2029.
Even December 2027 power delivery would leave little room for testing and commissioning before Oracle's deadline.
"In practice, a datacenter does not enter service as soon as first grid power arrives. Each building's electrical and cooling systems have to be energized, tested and commissioned before it can carry customer load. That will take time. We therefore expect the campus's load to ramp up mainly from the first quarter of 2028," Aterio said.
Meanwhile, the
Financial Times reported
that Tencent had signed a $7 billion deal to lease around 100,000 AI processors from Oracle.
For context, Oracle reported $55.7 billion in total capital expenditures for its fiscal 2026, which closed at the end of May. Its total revenue was $67.4 billion. Capex guidance for the 2027 financial year is up to $95 billion. ®

49934569.article_summary: 甲骨文威斯康星州AI数据中心“Project Lighthouse”可能延期，原因是连接电网所需的输电基础设施仍待监管批准。输电公司ATC已重新提交审批申请，预计部分供电最早于2027年10月、全面供电可能推迟至2028年甚至2029年，难以赶上甲骨文原定2027年下半年交付客户容量的计划。项目规模达902MW计算负载、总用电需求1.3GW，且甲骨文高额资本支出和新墨西哥项目的不可抗力通知进一步增加延期风险。
49934569.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Oracle数据中心建设受阻及其对客户、项目进度和公司执行能力的影响。

不同观点：
• **客户价值受损论**：JSR_FDED认为，Oracle客户支付的许可费用没有转化为更好的产品或支持，反而被用于资助不稳健的数据中心建设，质疑资金使用效率与客户回报。  
• **地方阻力加剧论**：bunderbunder指出，项目所在地Port Washington的公众反对声音强烈且不断扩大。项目每拖延一天，地方官员就可能获得更多机会设置阻碍，因此Oracle可能难以承受长期延误。  
• **执行与供应链失误论**：bpodgursky认为，Oracle将数据中心建设外包给反应迟缓的机构，对备用电源和电网接入缺乏预案，错误地假设并网会按常规推进。相比之下，Meta、OpenAI、Anthropic、SpaceX和Google更深度参与建设，因拥有内部核心团队而较少遭遇类似电力问题。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于项目受阻究竟主要源于地方政治和电力基础设施限制，还是Oracle外包管理不善、内部执行能力不足；评论整体对Oracle项目可靠性及其投资回报持怀疑态度。

data.title: Turbo Haskell
data.author: pjmlp
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了作者一周内开发的“Turbo Haskell Compiler（THC）”：基于Truffle/GraalVM，将GHC Core编译并运行于JVM，支持JIT与AOT、GHC原语、高级语言特性、C及多语言FFI、并发、异步异常、SIMD和高效尾调用。THC已能编译pandoc、happy、alex乃至GHC，并通过JVM优化提升性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 THC（面向 JVM、实现 GHC prim-ops 并提供 GHC Core JIT 的 Haskell 项目）的技术价值、命名、生态和项目可信度展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **技术认可**：有人认为项目很酷，尤其是 GraalVM 支持的多语言 FFI，适合实现“函数式核心、命令式外壳”；也有人分享作者接受 Haskell Interlude 采访的信息。  
• **命名与定位质疑**：评论者认为既然名称使用了“Turbo”，就应像 Turbo Pascal/Turbo Vision 一样提供 TUI IDE，否则命名不够贴切；另有人建议直接叫“Jaskell”。相关讨论也延伸到“IDE 是否可被视为某类 TUI”。  
• **同类项目联想**：有人提到 Frege——运行于 JVM 的 Haskell 方言，但其正式发布版本较旧，项目现状不明。  
• **功能与文档疑问**：有人注意到 FFI 列表没有 Java，认为这可能是疏漏；由于项目目标是 JVM，Java 支持缺失显得异常。  
• **对 Haskell 生态的疑问**：有人借“代理式编程”热潮发问：既然语言似乎不重要，为何不更多转向错误更少的 Haskell。  
• **质量与可信度争议**：有人质疑项目一周内约 4000 次提交，认为可能是 AI 生成的“代码垃圾”，怀疑作者是否真正理解底层实现；作者回应称项目正是自己一周前以玩笑起步，并反问评论者是否读过代理生成的项目说明。

补充讨论：部分用户无法访问网站，分别遭遇服务器找不到或杀毒软件拦截；文章还链接了 Reddit 讨论，可为相关疑问提供答案。

49921798.article_content:
On this page
Exactly a week ago (as a joke), I started writing THC, my “Turbo Haskell compiler,” while on vacation visiting
Bartosz Milewski
.
It has grown a tiny bit since then.
THC now implements every one of GHC 9.14.1’s prim-ops and provides a JIT for GHC Core that runs Haskell on the JVM. It uses the approach for running typed functional languages I developed several years ago in
Cadenza
(
talk
), using
Truffle
and
GraalVM
.
GHC still handles parsing, typechecking, desugaring, and Core optimization. THC takes over from there, compiling and executing that Core through its own runtime on Truffle/GraalVM. Advanced language features such as Template Haskell and Linear Haskell are fully supported.
While it can be used as a JIT for GHC-grade Haskell, it also supports ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation with Native Image, allowing it to produce executables.
THC is capable of JIT- or AOT-compiling a number of Haskell programs, including
pandoc
,
happy
,
alex
, and, as of today, even GHC itself!
THC resolves packages using Cabal and fully supports packages with multiple libraries, including Backpack.
Borrowing libraries
THC provides polyglot FFI to
Python
,
Ruby
,
R
, and
JavaScript
, letting Haskell raid libraries from other languages and bring their output straight into a JIT-compiled Haskell program. Conversion between
Data.Text
and Truffle strings over FFI is zero-copy for UTF-8-encoded strings inside other polyglot languages.
The idea is that if you need a data frame, want to run an LLM, or want a D3.js visualization, you should just pass
Text
out through foreign imports. Quasi-quotation-based
inline-<language name>
style bindings should be pretty easy to implement as well.
C/C++ bits in your Haskell libraries are run via FFI to native-mode
Sulong
(LLVM on the JVM). Managed-mode Sulong, where LLVM is interpreted inside the JVM and pointers are managed and garbage-collected, is also available, but is not used by the normal
foreign import
path.
Evaluation and concurrency
Internally, THC supports two different backends for Truffle evaluation: a bytecode-based JIT target and a traditional AST-based JIT target. Both can run in a single-threaded or multi-threaded style, with additional locking for the latter. It also supports GHC bytecode itself, so it can run BCO code as produced by GHCi.
THC fully supports
throwTo
, asynchronous exceptions that leave behind resumable code, and masking.
THC supports both “normal” Java threading and
Project Loom
, upon which it offers lightweight GHC-style green threading with a HEC-style runtime executor permitting cheap
MVar
s and the like.
SIMD
THC supports SIMD using the relatively limited supply of available GHC prim-ops, but it can also go further, allowing runtime selection of the SIMD “species” width and JIT-compiling loops using that information through the incubating
Vector API
(
jdk.incubator.vector
). This lets the JIT start to earn its keep!
In fact, nothing prevents the runtime from providing complete
RuntimeRep
-polymorphic code at runtime other than the fact that we have no Core that takes advantage of that freedom!
Tail calls
Hot tail calls become loops. When execution has to fall back to ordinary calls, THC periodically unwinds the accumulated stack frames.
Previous efforts to run functional code on the JVM, such as the
Eta programming language
and the design I used with Runar Bjarnason for trampolining Scalaz’s monads, used a trampoline mechanism. THC instead uses a code transformation trick to keep hot tail calls inside tight basic-block-style loops with side exits.
During recursion in tracing mode, THC fills a 64-bit
Bloom filter
to detect likely recursive tail calls. When it finds a likely hit, it throws a slow-path exception to connect the continuation with the launch site, and then custom Truffle nodes get Graal to transform the current tail-call loop across function bodies into a tight loop. False positives mean extra slow-path work; they don’t change the program’s result.
When later code paths diverge, THC tries to grow additional side loops, like a tracing JIT, until it hits the JVM’s limits on function body size. At that point, it’ll finally spill a tail call in a way that “leaks” a stack frame.
That leak is temporary. We can compact the accumulated stack frames using a trick somewhat similar to
CHICKEN Scheme’s garbage collection strategy
, reusing the machinery we needed to support resumable code in the presence of asynchronous exceptions. The result is that hot loops can run
very
hot indeed.
When benchmarking
Data.Map
in particular, I found it needed something like 66 fallback trampoline calls compared to several million fast-path calls.
Performance
The runtime can also use
compressed ordinary object pointers (compressed oops)
. These represent heap references as 32-bit offsets rather than full 64-bit pointers, reducing the memory occupied by references and helping more data fit in cache. With the JVM’s usual 8-byte object alignment, this limits the he

data.title: Shimano Bicycle Museum Review
data.author: pietroppeter
data.article_summary: 文章介绍日本关西的禧玛诺自行车博物馆。博物馆以自行车发展史和多样用途为核心，展出从早期木马车到现代赛车、山地车、残奥会用车及日常自行车，并通过互动展台讲解材料、结构和社会背景。馆内虽有禧玛诺产品及发展资料，却不过度强调企业史，还设有图书馆和研究档案，整体兼具观赏性与教育意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕自行车博物馆及自行车、Shimano技术与骑行文化展开，兼有参观推荐、历史兴趣和个人经历分享。

不同观点：
• **博物馆值得参观**：有人强烈推荐湾区 Marin 自行车博物馆，认为其展示了从直接脚踏到现代设计的演变，包括转向、变速、链条、刹车等“失败的进化路线”，并特别强调山地车的发展史。日本大阪附近的读者得知后表示想去，计划赴日的骑行者则询问其适合什么类型的观众、是否值得绕道参观。  
• **自行车历史与收藏价值**：评论提到乌克兰哈尔科夫自行车厂及荷兰自行车博物馆，说明讨论不限于Shimano，也关注不同国家的自行车工业、老车和技术演化。  
• **认同机械工程与Shimano产品**：有人因给Shimano Tourney上油而感受到精密工程的魅力；山地车用户称赞XT/XTR曲柄、碟刹和锁踏，认为Shimano产品可靠、持续改进。也有人特别期待博物馆展出2004年首代十速Dura-Ace，认为其性能和精度是重大跃升。  
• **骑行文化与专业内容**：有人推荐专业自行车评论、书评和著名赛段游记；韩国、日本骑行经历者则称赞博物馆工作人员友善。  
• **跨领域联想与个人回忆**：部分评论把Shimano延伸到其渔具（鱼竿、鱼轮）业务，玩笑称自行车展中缺少渔具；另有人分享少年时代Shimano自行车被盗、至今难忘的经历。

补充讨论：争议不大，焦点主要是博物馆的定位和参观价值，以及Shimano自行车技术与渔具业务之间的联想。

49930047.article_content:
A look at the Shimano Bike Museum with praise for its focus on bicycles over its own corporate history. For anyone in the Kansai area of Japan, perhaps visiting Kyoto or Osaka, this has a prodigious collections of machines and within a well-designed setting.
The museum itself is striking, a modern building that’s glass and steel. To see pictures of it online is to imagine it might be Shimano’s head office in a prime location, and that there’s a museum inside. However it is all museum, and the surrounding area more ordinary.
“In Japanese, we call a bicycle “jitensha,” which literally means “wheels rotated by oneself.” This means a bicycle is operated by the rider and that there are as many ways of enjoying cycling as there are riders.”
This English text is from the welcome message written on the wall at the start of the museum tour. You might learn the word for bicycle here as you enter, by the time you leave the message of many ways to enjoy cycling will come through. The sign is of course in Japanese too and the museum is bilingual.
Head upstairs and you enter a large darkened room with a procession of bicycles under spotlights. These cover the chronology of the machine, from rudimentary hobby horses to the arrival of pedals, the chain, tires more evolution. This large space also doubles as an auditorium and an educational film is played at times that covers the history of the bicycle and the origins of cycle sport too, all within a wider societal context that touches on war, industrialisation and consumerism.
Then it’s into a bright white room where frosted glass lets in daylight and more spotlights highlight exhibits such as Freddy Maerten’s steel Flandria. You can get close to touch it – not that you would or should – but it’s not behind glass or roped off, just raised on a small stage. You can see the Ishiwata tubing decal and the Shimano Crane rear mech, the beginnings of Shimano in the pro peloton. All the other bikes are similarly accessible. You can see bikes used at Paralympic games and notice the custom modifications up close. A Breezer, one of the first mountain bikes to go on sale, sits there and you can spot a Campagnolo headset and motorbike brake levers among the components on the “clunker”.
As well as history there’s the humdrum. A Crescent bike in the yellow and blue of the Swedish postal service, complete with studded tires to show you can ride on ice, even with a heavy cargo. A very much used Cannondale is loaded with luggage, spare tires wrapped around the bags like boa constrictors, and all caked in dust, as if Tatsu Sakimoto had come in and parked it mid-way during his four year, 55,000km journey around the world. A Merida bike from the 2021 Olympics road race is there, complete with scratches galore and crash dents. The event
feels like yesterday
but the bike already looks ancient. Plenty of kids bikes feature too, shopping bikes and more. Everyone ought to recognise something they’ve ridden.
Stands explores materials science with a comparison of steel, aluminium and titanium tubing and the chance to feel the weight of these metals yourself. Another lets you pick up racing bike to feel how light it is. But among all this educational material is the simple message that bikes can do plenty.
It’s actually hard to find much about Shimano and its origins here. There’s a mention that gun blacksmiths in Sakai started repairing imported bikes in the late 19th century and soon began manufacture. For what it’s worth the city Sakai has long been a big steel production area, first for swords and then into other goods including guns and cutlery. It’s here that Shimano started too but it’s only later and in passing that you come across a small item that was Shimano’s first product: a freewheel.
Shozaburo Shimano founded the company to make these and one thing led to another. Including fishing freewheels and gearing can be applied inside reels and today one quarter of Shimano’s revenue coming from fishing tackle, about a billion Euros, comes from fishing but there’s not a rod nor reel in sight.
Still the museum is visibly the Shimano museum in other ways. There’s excellent stand where a racing bike has been broken into pieces, apparently there are 3,200 parts in one bike if you really count every chain pin, bolt and electronic circuit component. Of course it’s a Shimano Dura-Ace groupset in the display. Good luck finding SRAM or Campagnolo but there are a few examples, even a Mavic rear mech.
The top floor of the museum includes also a set of display cases for the flagship Dura-Ace and XTR groups starting with the 1973 version, then 1984, 1996, 2004, 2012, 2016, 2021, complete with four empty displays waiting to house 2027 and the rest of what the future brings.
There’s also a library and behind this, a locked archive for researchers. This is valuable, the museum might house one of each type of bike but here the shelves are full of books, brochures and catalogues. A treasure of primary source mater

data.title: A 12-year sequence of telescope images of a star and four planets orbiting
data.author: mariuz
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕直接成像的系外行星轨道动画，讨论其真实性、制作方法、科学意义、观测局限及未来技术。

不同观点：
• 技术与数据：wthomp展示仅使用凯克望远镜、同一仪器和3.5微米波段制作的动画；原GIF则综合了不同望远镜和波长。  
• 真实性争议：hatthew指出动画只有约10张静态图，其余数百帧为插值生成，并非连续实拍；但仍具有展示价值。  
• 观测前景：ortusdux期待罗曼空间望远镜日冕仪，称其灵敏度将提升100—1000倍，可直接拍摄类似木星的行星；7373737373补充宜居世界天文台未来或能发现类地行星。  
• 科学意义：alexpotato指出现代搜寻技术已将“拥有行星的恒星比例”从原先低估修正到接近100%；sixothree以科学史变化强调系外行星发现的突破。  
• 公众传播：tocs3认为科学图像虽未必总是研究重点，却是非专业公众理解科学的重要途径；其他评论推荐银河系中心恒星绕黑洞运行等相关动画。

补充讨论：评论者还追问观测间隔、恒星遮挡噪声变化、行星角距，以及是否存在被大型行星“遮蔽”的更小行星；争议焦点主要是动画的“实拍程度”及图像变化究竟源于天体活动还是观测技术改进。

• 观测前景：ortusdux期待罗曼空间望远镜日冕仪，称其灵敏度将提升100—1000倍，可直接拍摄类似木星的行星；7373737373补充宜居世界天文台未来或能发现类地行星。  
• 科学意义：alexpotato指出现代搜寻技术已将“拥有行星的恒星比例”从原先低估修正到接近100%；sixothree以科学史变化强调系外行星发现的突破。  
• 公众传播：tocs3认为科学图像虽未必总是研究重点，却是非专业公众理解科学的重要途径；其他评论推荐银河系中心恒星绕黑洞运行等相关动画。

补充讨论：评论者还追问观测间隔、恒星遮挡噪声变化、行星角距，以及是否存在被大型行星“遮蔽”的更小行星；争议焦点主要是动画的“实拍程度”及图像变化究竟源于天体活动还是观测技术改进。
