49933869.article_content:
The forgetful CPU (Linux on
M4)
This blog post goes into quite some detail about how I first
booted Linux on my M4 Mac mini. I encourage you to look up terms and
concepts you don’t know, since I cannot explain all the background in
this post ;)
Before saying anything further, I need to thank the entire
Asahi Linux
team for all their prior
work and help during the journey. Please consider donating to the
Asahi Open Collective
if you want to see more mainline Linux on Apple Silicon work!
The Beginnings
In November 2024, I bought an M4 Mac mini, gambling that it would be
similar to the M1-M3 Apple Silicon machines and could be quickly
supported in Asahi Linux. While the M4 was sitting on my desk for
several months, more details started surfacing about this SoC.
It turned out to be more difficult, since the M4 machines are the first
generation of Apple Silicon to mandate SPTM (Secure Page Table Monitor),
which provides hardening against vulnerabilities in the XNU kernel of
macOS. In previous generations, the Linux bringup was largely based on
MMIO traces captured using the m1n1 hypervisor, allowing the analysis of
interactions between the original macOS drivers and the hardware. With
SPTM, major changes to m1n1 are required to get macOS running under the
hypervisor, and these changes certainly go beyond what I could come up
with as a newbie in this space.
Still, it wasn’t entirely a lost cause. In parallel to the hypervisor
work, I started my first attempts to boot Linux on the M4. This meant
disabling strict boot security, installing m1n1 as a custom boot object
via macOS recovery
1
, and obtaining a serial console
2
to inspect the logs.
Locked registers
Initially, m1n1 was only able to start in BRINGUP mode and
immediately crashed while attempting to initialize GXF
3
otherwise. GXF functionality turned out to be disabled/locked in raw
boot mode on these M4+ SoCs, so making its initialization conditional
and skipping it on these machines was the correct thing to do. Besides
the disabled GXF feature, there was also the RVBAR (Reset Vector Base
Address Register): a place in memory (one per CPU core) that determines
where the core starts executing when powered on. The m1n1 code writes
its entrypoint address to the RVBAR for each core when booting the
kernel or chainloading another m1n1. Writing to it also led to a crash
on M4, but long story short, it already contained the correct value so
this write needed to be skipped as well.
2024-12-01 17:37 <yuka> can confirm this state gives a working usb proxy, as in a "Generic m1n1 uartproxy v1.4.17-61-ga24ff77" turns up in lsusb, and I can open a shell :)
debug_putc
At this point, a long time went by without me touching the Mac mini. At
the Chaos Communication Congress at the end of 2025, I found some new
motivation. Finally, I hacked together a very minimal device tree
containing only the CPU cores and AIC interrupt controller and loaded
the Linux kernel (using m1n1’s
linux.py
) with the
earlycon
parameter, but I did not see any output after
“Vectoring to next stage”. Since I wasn’t getting any useful output from
the kernel, I could only take wild guesses at what was going wrong,
right? I decided to try the brute-force method: good old
println
-debugging. I took the
debug_putc
assembly routine from m1n1 and adjusted it to print a single ‘a’
character
4
. I inserted this into the Linux
kernel code very early in boot, and sure enough, I got an ‘a’ after
“Vectoring to next stage”! Essentially, I bisected the Linux boot code
and landed at the MMU init code (which is still
very
early,
still in the assembly code in
arch/arm64/kernel/head.S
).
Was the MMU initialization crashing the CPU somehow? Not quite: the UART
is accessed using memory-mapped I/O. Once the MMU is enabled, all memory
accesses are directed to virtual addresses, which are mapped to a
corresponding physical addresses through the page-tables. While m1n1
creates mappings to expose the MMIO address space at identical virtual
addresses, Linux does not do this, meaning we end up accessing unmapped
space instead of the UART once the MMU is enabled. I modified the
initial pagetables to add this 1:1 mapping for the MMIO space, and now
my
debug_putc
worked much further into the boot process.
Bisecting again, the print now worked up to somewhere in the interrupt
controller initialization! I narrowed it down to a write to the
implementation-specific CPU register
SYS_IMP_APL_VM_TMR_FIQ_ENA_EL2
, which triggered the new
crash. After I commented out this write, the kernel booted to a shell.
Let’s goooo!
SYS_IMP_APL_VM_TMR_FIQ_ENA_EL2
, which is
related to virtualization, has since been unlocked in new iBoot
versions, so commenting out the write is no longer necessary.
Now that I knew that Linux code was actually being executed, I looked
once again into why I hadn’t gotten any
printk
output on
the serial console earlier despite the
earlycon
boot
parameter.
2026-01-23 12:35 <yuka> added earlycon=s5l,0x3ad200000 to my bootarg

data.title: Things That Apparently Cause Cancer
data.author: timpera
data.article_summary: 文章质疑哈佛研究以居民与核电站的地理距离推断癌症风险的做法。作者认为“接近”不等于实际辐射暴露，研究存在生态谬误、混淆变量和因果推断缺陷。通过复现并套用到仓库、大学、体育场等地标，几乎都能得出“导致癌症”的荒谬结论，说明该方法无法证明核电站造成癌症。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕核设施附近居民癌症风险研究及相关证据评述，讨论流行病学关联能否支持因果结论，以及评论文章是否存在立场偏向。

不同观点：
• **支持该文章者**：fliglr表示喜欢这篇关于“X是否导致Y”的证据综述，倾向认可其分析框架。  
• **强调谨慎解读流行病学证据者**：dekhn指出癌症研究通常只能表明“风险关联”，不能轻易说“证明因果”。附近电厂、道路或机场工作者的癌症率升高，可能受到社会经济地位等混杂因素影响；但混杂因素也不能自动排除环境暴露的可能。  
• **反对单一生物机制推断者**：dekhn认为，不能因为尚未明确DNA损伤机制，就断定辐射不会致癌。冷却塔排放、下风向传播等仍可能构成暴露途径；工人采取防护措施，也不代表周边居民没有风险。癌症成因和生物物理机制本身十分复杂。  
• **质疑文章客观性者**：dekhn指出作者及其所在突破研究所与核能推广存在利益关联，可能影响论证立场；forgetfreeman则更直接地将该文章斥为“赤裸裸的宣传”。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于：相关性是否足以支持因果推断、应如何处理混杂变量与未知机制，以及作者的核能立场是否削弱文章可信度。

49940219.article_content:
Things that Apparently Cause Cancer
What does this methodology measure anyway?
Deric Tilson
and
Adam Stein
Oct 02, 2026
55
3
15
Share
It would shock you to know that Costco, according to a new Harvard School of Public Health methodology, caused 120,687 cases of cancer mortality nationally every year, simply due to living in close proximity to their warehouses. Private colleges accounted for 83,782 more. Harvard itself is responsible for 5,842 cancer deaths. Living near a Major League Baseball field causes almost 19 times as many cancer deaths as living near a Major League Soccer pitch. These conclusions are obviously absurd, but they come from the exact same methodology that researchers at Harvard use to “prove” that nuclear power plants cause cancer in nearby communities.
Earlier this year, Adam Stein and I called out a series of Harvard studies showing that nuclear power plants were associated with higher rates of cancer incidence and cancer mortality as nonsense. Now that we’ve spent the last few months replicating the analysis and expanding it, we are able to show that no matter what landmark you use, their methodology will show an increased cancer risk and mortality. The studies simply do not prove anything about cancer incidence.
Let’s recap: In December 2025, researchers led by Yazan Alwadi at Harvard’s T.H. Chan School of Public Health published a
paper
in
Environmental Health
that claimed to find that cancer incidence increased for people living closer to nuclear power plants in Massachusetts. In March, the same researchers published an expanded nationwide
study
claiming a similar result—this time looking at cancer mortality rates, rather than incidence—in
Nature Communications
. This was followed by a
paper
in the
Journal of Exposure Science & Environmental Epidemiology
that looked at associations of lung, breast, and colon cancers. Most recently, a
study
of total mortality, not just cancer, was published in the European journal
Environmental Epidemiology
.
The papers construct a “proximity score” based on distance from nuclear plants, up to 120 km in Massachusetts and 200 km in the national studies (about 75 and 125 miles). Every ZIP code or county inside those radii is treated as exposed, with closer locations receiving higher weights. If a ZIP code or county is within range of multiple sites, then the effect is cumulative. That means that a county that is in close proximity to one nuclear power plant could have a smaller score than another county that is further away from any one power plant but within range of many.
From this proximity score, the authors run regressions testing the outcome (cancer incidence, cancer mortality, or total mortality) on the proximity of the county and a collection of covariates. From this, they use the statistical coefficients, construct the Relative Risk for each county, age, and sex group, and compute the Attributable Fraction, from which they derive the number of attributed deaths from the nuclear power plant from 2000 to 2018. The authors state that their methodology and results provide the scientific basis and public health justification for an expanded research program.
But proximity is not exposure. We have methods of measuring exposure for nuclear power plant workers. While the radiation exposure of nuclear workers will always be greater than or equal to that received by the surrounding public, most of the closely monitored US nuclear workforce
receive no measurable annual dose
. When workers are exposed to radiation, the average dose received is only 2 percent of the occupational limit. If operators and workers who are on-site at nuclear power plants receive an annual dose between zero and one-fiftieth of the occupational limit, how is it possible that residents 5, 10, 25, 50, 120, or 200 kilometers away would receive any measurable dose from the same plant?
In talks, the authors hedge that their papers are merely ecological studies that show association, but never prove causality. Ecological studies are used to understand the relationship between outcome and exposure at a population level. This leads us to ask: what would the mechanism of exposure be? Well, according to the authors, we can just ignore the broader literature and physics, and instead make up exposure pathways and mechanisms. The use of an “ecological study” allows a lot of leeway in terms of explaining the broader world.
Over the last several months, we have replicated the results of these papers. The authors supplied us with eight lines of code and answered a couple of questions about the covariates, which did not replicate the results. Most of our replication was done through first principles combined with trial and error. Once we were reasonably close to the results of the first national study on cancer mortality, we took the methodology and applied it to numerous other landmarks.

data.title: Apple Pass Designer
data.author: soheilpro
data.article_summary: Pass Designer是苹果推出的电子凭证设计工具，支持健身卡、门票、登机牌等多种通行证。用户可使用模板和自定义图片创建设计，实时预览其在iPhone及Apple Watch上的效果，调整颜色与布局并编辑标准字段。工具还提供实时验证、语义标签和向后兼容功能，便于接入Siri、日历和地图。测试版需macOS 27或更高版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple 推出 Pass Designer 的意义、实用性、推出时机及技术设计。

不同观点：
• 低门槛且合理：有人认为这是过去难以优先开发、如今借助 LLM 很容易实现的工具；数据结构清晰、无需复杂交互，主要编码成本已大幅降低，因此并不“有趣”，但仍是实用产品。
• 实用但姗姗来迟：支持者指出 Wallet Pass 可用于会员卡、优惠券、票券等多种场景，普通用户也能创建；但 Apple 早年文档不足，制作 PKPASS 很麻烦，因而有人认为该功能晚了约十年。
• 地区与用户差异：有人觉得它对旧金山等数字化程度高的地区更有意义；也有人已将其用于英国 Lidl 等实体卡场景。
• 生态扩展：评论提到 iOS 27 Wallet 已支持扫描现有条码/二维码生成 Pass；也有人建议把 Pass、图标等设计工具整合为开发者工作室，或加入生成式 AI 自动融合条码与视觉设计。
• 技术疑问与建议：有人质疑 PKPASS 是否存在签名、验证等门槛；另建议让 Pass 语义化标记条码区域，仅提高该区域亮度，避免扫描时整块屏幕刺眼。macOS 27 的系统要求也引发疑问。

补充讨论：已有第三方网页工具和“Offline Cards”等替代方案，说明需求长期存在；争议焦点主要是功能本身是否重要，以及 Apple 推出是否过晚。

49937276.article_content:
Introducing Pass Designer
Whether you’re creating passes for a local fitness center, a small music venue, a global airline, or a national coffee chain, Pass Designer makes it easy to craft and preview passes that reflect your business.
Building passes made easy
Start with templates provided by Apple or your own to capture the personality of your brand. You can use your preferred design tool to create images for passes — such as logos, backgrounds, or strip images — then bring them into Pass Designer to complete a pass design.
As you edit, Pass Designer updates the preview in real time to show how a pass will appear on iPhone and Apple Watch. The preview uses the same rendering as iOS and watchOS, so what you see in Pass Designer is exactly what customers will see on their device.
Colors and appearance
Easily adjust a pass’s background, foreground, and label colors.
Adaptable layouts
Pass Designer supports designs that take full advantage of the latest advances in Apple Wallet, as well as backward-compatible passes.
Standard fields
Each pass type includes standard fields for displaying information, and you can edit each field’s content directly in Pass Designer.
Validation
Pass Designer validates your pass as you work and alerts you to any issues such as missing required key values and unexpected definitions.
Semantic tags
For boarding passes and event tickets, semantic tags add structured data — such as event dates, venue locations, or flight details — that the system uses to enable features like Siri Suggestions, Calendar integration, and Maps directions.
Pass Designer lets you edit semantic tags directly in the UI, and you can view a semantic and non-semantic pass side by side. It can also automatically generate a backward-compatible pass structure from your semantic data that doesn’t require semantic tags, ensuring your pass works where they may not be supported.
Download the beta
Pass Designer beta requires macOS 27 or later. To download, sign in with your Apple Account. If prompted, complete the free registration and accept the Apple Developer Agreement.

• 技术疑问与建议：有人质疑 PKPASS 是否存在签名、验证等门槛；另建议让 Pass 语义化标记条码区域，仅提高该区域亮度，避免扫描时整块屏幕刺眼。macOS 27 的系统要求也引发疑问。

补充讨论：已有第三方网页工具和“Offline Cards”等替代方案，说明需求长期存在；争议焦点主要是功能本身是否重要，以及 Apple 推出是否过晚。

data.title: Court agrees with EFF: Utah's VPN law demands a technical impossibility
data.author: hn_acker
data.article_summary: 美国犹他州SB73要求成人网站识别并阻断使用VPN的用户、进行年龄验证，甚至禁止提供绕过指南。EFF认为该法侵犯隐私、造成州外用户和企业负担，并要求技术上不可能的精准定位。联邦法官据此发布初步禁令，暂缓执行相关条款，认定其可能违宪。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：犹他州要求网站验证用户年龄、限制VPN绕过访问的法律，是否可行、合法，以及州政府管辖互联网的边界。

不同观点：
• 技术不可行论：VPN流量难以可靠识别，用户可通过普通云主机、自建隧道或代理绕过；按域名过滤也容易失效。有人认为该法要求“技术不可能”，立法者缺乏技术常识。  
• 可执行论：反驳者指出，DraftKings等赌博网站能通过账户、支付和位置验证限制特定州用户，因此并非完全无法实施，但自建VPN等方式仍很难封堵。  
• 自由与宪法争议：禁止网站提供VPN绕过教程被质疑侵犯第一修正案；也有人认为州无权管辖州外服务器，需挑战其互联网管辖权。  
• 反审查立场：有人警告这是政府扩大网络控制的开端，色情限制只是表面理由；“互联网总会绕过审查”并非定律，中国、伊朗等案例表明监控、自我审查和SNI封锁能有效压制访问，维护开放网络需要主动行动。  
• 州政策辩护：犹他州禁赌，限制VPN以执行赌博禁令在逻辑上自洽；支持者称赌博会带来成瘾、债务、家庭暴力和治安问题，因此州应有一定执法空间。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于公共利益与个人网络自由的平衡，以及州级法律能否、是否应当跨越技术和地域边界执行。

49927754.article_content:
Español
When state lawmakers attempt to rewrite how the internet works, users rely on courts to recognize that laws can’t make technical impossibilities a reality. That’s why we were happy to see that a court has blocked Utah’s attempt to outlaw the privacy protections of Virtual Private Networks (VPNs).
In a win for digital rights, a federal judge has
issued a preliminary injunction
blocking Utah’s SB 73, the state’s draconian
anti-VPN age verification law
. The decision comes as EFF
submitted our comments
to the Utah Department of Commerce, detailing how forcing platforms to detect and block privacy-preserving tools undermines user privacy and security worldwide while demanding the impossible.
What SB 73 Does
Signed
into law earlier this year
, SB 73 attempted to regulate adult websites by requiring them to block VPN users or to identify the physical location of visitors using them or similar tools that mask their network traffic. It even went so far as to prohibit websites from offering instructions on how to use a VPN to bypass these checks. This made Utah, to EFF’s knowledge, the first state in the nation to target the use of VPNs to avoid legally mandated age-verification gates.
The Utah federal court
halted enforcement
of the law's VPN provisions last week,
r
uling that the law likely violates the U.S. Constitution’s prohibition on passing laws that significantly burden businesses and people outside Utah’s borders.
SB 73 burdens the rights of all internet users outside of Utah because it requires adult websites to either know every visiting user’s physical location, and then block those in Utah, or to verify every visitor’s age just in case they might be in Utah. The law’s “actual-location provision in practice requires an entity to perform age verification services for every user visiting its site from any location because the entity would violate the law if even one of those users happened to be obfuscating,” the court wrote. The court essentially ruled that Utah has less-burdensome ways to prevent Utah minors from accessing adult websites than requiring all users in the world to comply with SB 73.
Aylo’s lawsuit does not challenge SB 73’s provision prohibiting the websites covered by the law from sharing information about VPNs.
The Legal Challenge
This court order follows months of legal maneuvering.
Initially set to
go into effect in May 2026
, SB 73 sparked an
immediate constitutional challenge from Aylo
, the parent company of major online adult platforms like Pornhub. In response to the lawsuit, Utah and Aylo
initially agreed
that the state would pause enforcement while the court considered the preliminary injunction request
or
until administrative rules setting specific compliance terms were finalized. Those proposed compliance rules (R152-78B, see
Utah State Bulletin, page 6
) were published by the Utah Department of Commerce’s Division of Consumer Protection on September 1
st
, and EFF
submitted formal comments
to the Department in opposition. According to the notice, the proposed rules could be effective as soon as October 8, 2026. However, Judge Barlow’s decision means that it cannot be enforced pending further action by the court.
The Ruling
EFF welcomes Judge Barlow’s ruling, which recognizes the fundamental disconnect between state legislation of the internet and how technology works. In his ruling, Judge Barlow noted that the statute requires a technical impossibility on pain of legal liability. “Aylo is correct that the statute, as amended, now essentially imposes strict liability for entities like it when it comes to determining the location of its websites’ users.”
The court recognized that the problem is that SB 73 “requires entities like Aylo to geolocate its website users with perfection to avoid liability.” But, at the same time, the court acknowledged “that geolocation perfection is not presently possible.”
EFF explained this technical impossibility in
our comment to the Department of Commerce.
VPNs protect user privacy by routing web traffic through intermediary servers. Because destination websites only see the IP address of the VPN server, they have no reliable mechanism to tell whether a connection originates from Salt Lake City, Seattle, or Shanghai. So, under Utah's current statutory framework, platforms are left with an impossible choice: completely block all VPN traffic nationwide or withdraw access from Utah entirely. Judge Barlow agreed, asserting:
Because the law requires perfection in the absence of perfect geolocation tools, Aylo would need to verify those 28 million users—whether located in Salt Lake City, Boston, New Orleans, Anchorage, or Honolulu—to ensure compliance and avoid liability.
The Rulemaking
The administrative rules drafted by the state compelled commercial entities to implement "commercially reasonable geolocation obfuscation detection systems", which is a directive, we argue, that demands a technical impossibility.

data.title: Mike Tomlin spent 12 years building a Minecraft city
data.author: CoryOndrejka
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：前NFL教练迈克·汤姆林花12年在《我的世界》中用手柄建造城市，引发对个人兴趣、创造意义、投入方式及其职业表现的讨论。

不同观点：
• 多数评论赞赏其投入与真诚，认为即使不懂《我的世界》或橄榄球，也能感受到长期创作带来的快乐；有人称其“感人、温暖”，甚至建议匹兹堡聘他做城市规划顾问。  
• 有人强调作品的意义不在技术难度。虽然熟练玩家、程序或AI可能更快生成类似城市，但这是他在自身限制下亲手完成、体现个人思想的作品，可视为AI时代“为兴趣而做”的例子。  
• 也有人钦佩其耐心：他使用手柄且灵敏度较低，耗时可能是PC操作的两倍；考虑到他曾是长期保持胜绩的NFL主教练，这种业余投入尤其不可思议。  
• 调侃或质疑其职业取舍的观点认为，他开始建城后季后赛战绩从5胜3负降至3胜9负，球员甚至开玩笑说球队在争超级碗时教练却在玩Minecraft。  
• 部分玩家更偏好自动化，认为重复建造繁琐，AI或模组可生成主体、让孩子添加细节，但这可能破坏生存模式的平衡。

补充讨论：评论借电影台词讨论“何时回归真正让自己快乐的事”，并批评“成年人玩游戏很丢脸”的社会偏见；也有人认为若基本生活有保障，人们或许能更多从事这类非功利创作。

data.title: Loss of cell identity drives human aging: Two new papers
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕胚胎表观遗传重置及相关论文，讨论衰老是否可逆、其机制是损伤积累还是进化编程，以及研究的局限。

不同观点：
• **表观遗传重置支持部分可逆性**：胚胎受精后可清除父源DNA上的年龄相关化学标记、重塑染色质、重建端粒并清理受损蛋白，但无法修复精子累积的DNA突变；有人据此将生物系统理解为“信息系统”。
• **强调证据边界**：线粒体重置主要针对父源线粒体；母源线粒体通常不会被重置，少数父源线粒体遗传的影响仍不清楚。
• **质疑“损伤/漂移”模型**：有评论认为论文只是给累积损伤假说换了包装，未解释Hayflick极限、不同物种寿命差异等，并主张衰老和死亡是为适应进化而被程序化的核心机制。
• **折中或相反假说**：表观遗传衰老可能是对DNA损伤的适应性、程序化反应，类似病毒症状主要由免疫反应造成，而非病毒直接造成。

补充讨论：有人指出慢性压力可能加速衰老，并询问定点甲基化/去甲基化技术；也有人认为研究忽略了连接不同时间尺度的昼夜节律。另有评论关注论文未充分讨论新的Hayflick极限，以及批评网页使用AI插图而削弱信息价值。

data.title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI until now
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 卡内基梅隆、MIT等机构研发的AI Ataraxos在战略棋（Stratego）中以15胜1负4和击败顶尖棋手。该棋信息隐藏多、局势复杂且棋局漫长，长期难以被AI攻克。Ataraxos通过1.63亿局自我对弈、动态调整学习步幅，并利用“信念模型”预测对手隐藏棋子、搜索可能局面，形成冷静、擅长 bluff 和逆转的策略。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在含隐藏信息的《Stratego（战略家）》中达到超越顶尖人类水平的原因、意义与局限。

不同观点：
• 多数评论认为，Ataraxos的关键突破是更高效地学习预测对手行为；隐藏棋子使传统“向前搜索”困难，策略取决于不可见信息，类似不可预测的石头剪刀布。  
• 有人强调其成果：仅用约16块GPU、数千美元，训练对局数约为DeepNash的1/34，却以15胜1负4和击败顶尖棋手，说明2022年DeepMind所谓“掌握”仍不充分。  
• 也有人指出，成果离不开CMU、MIT、纽约大学和斯坦福等多校团队，不应简单理解为低成本、轻松实现。  
• 玩家从实战角度讨论策略：AI把旗帜藏在角落、仅用两枚炸弹保护，属于少见但有效的布局；游戏核心还包括强子力棋子的安全调动、心理战和虚张声势。  
• 有评论认为固定规则的Stratego较易被反复训练；若是持续更新卡牌的游戏，新内容会破坏训练数据，且决策树更复杂，AI可能更难适应。

补充讨论：评论提到Hanabi等不完全信息游戏也适用类似方法，并关注“静默防御”规则因信息更少，可能对AI构成更大挑战；另有玩家分享童年经历及作弊导致的信息泄露。

Deep Blue took down Garry Kasparov at chess in 1997, AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol at Go in 2016, and poker bots have been beating professionals for years. But one classic game called
Stratego
held out. Even DeepMind, with its exceptional budget, couldn’t build a machine that reliably beat the best human players.
Now, a team of researchers from Carnegie Mellon, MIT, New York University, and Stanford University has done it. Their AI, called Ataraxos, beat Pim Niemeijer, arguably the best
Stratego
player of all time, 15 games to one, with four draws. And it took just 16 GPUs and a few thousand dollars to train it.
Hidden armies
In
Stratego
, each player gets 40 pieces representing military ranks, from a marshal down to a spy, plus bombs and a flag. You win by capturing the opponent’s flag. Your opponent knows
where
your pieces are, but not
what
they are. Identities are revealed only when two pieces collide in battle—the weaker one is removed, and the identity of the winner is revealed. That makes
Stratego
an imperfect-information game, just like poker, which computers cracked years ago. “There’s something super distinctive about
Stratego
, which is that it is a massive amount of hidden information that unfolds over a very long time scale,” said Eugene Vinitsky, a researcher at NYU and co-author of the study.
In some forms of poker, the hidden information is tiny. In Texas Hold’em, “You only have two hidden cards,” said Gabriele Farina, an MIT computer scientist and another co-author. That leaves just 1,326 possible hands, few enough for a machine to weigh them all. “In
Stratego
, there’s 40 pieces on the board that could be in any order,” Farina said. That’s more than a decillion possible setups. Then there’s the game’s length.
“In chess, usually the game lasts 40 moves, but in
Stratego
, a game can easily last 2,000 moves,” Farina said. On top of that,
Stratego
is a game of bluffing. Sometimes you move a weak piece as if it were a marshal, just to scare the opponent off. When players bluff too often, their threats mean nothing; when they never bluff, they become predictable. That balancing act, the team explains, is what stumped earlier AIs like DeepMind’s DeepNash, introduced in 2022.
Learning to guess
Just like DeepNash, Ataraxos learned by playing against itself—163 million games in total. In these self-play sessions, moves that led to wins were reinforced and played more often in future matches, while moves that led to losses were played less, which was the same simple training idea. The difference was in how much Ataraxos adjusted after each game, because hidden information tends to send self-play learning algorithms around in circles. The team addressed this by making big, bold changes in strategy early in training and small, careful ones later.
The even bigger innovation was something DeepNash never had: thinking ahead before each move. AIs like AlphaGo refine their general strategy with a search just before acting. DeepMind couldn’t make that work in
Stratego
because the search space was too large, leaving it an open question whether it was worth trying.
“This is one of the things that we did figure out how to do,” Farina said. The solution was a second neural network, a belief model, trained to guess the opponent’s hidden pieces based on how they had been moving. This way, instead of iterating through every possible arrangement, Ataraxos samples plausible ones, plays out candidate moves in each, and picks based on how they turned out.
And it shows in its playstyle.
Calm and unbothered
The name Ataraxos comes from the ancient Greek word for a state of calm. “It means somebody that’s calm and unbothered,” Farina explained. He suggests the structure of the AI and its lack of human emotions ensure it doesn’t react impulsively, “even in situations where a human would be losing their mind.” While the human might try big gambles to come back from a significant deficit, Ataraxos would work its way back into the game slowly and methodically.
The strategy it developed also avoids drawing attention to any problems it faces. When Ataraxos estimates its opponent has no reason to suspect a weak spot, it leaves that spot alone, even if it might look like a disaster waiting to happen to anyone who can see both sides of the board.
“For humans, it’s very hard when you know a secret to make decisions ignoring the fact that you know that secret,” Farina said. “For machines, it’s easy.” This, the team says, leads machines to make moves a human would only do while bluffing—and follow up on them much better than humans. “We would watch the bot ‘bluff’ its way back from like a two percent victory probability, very, very casually,” Vinitsky added.

49933740.article_summary: 卡内基梅隆、MIT等机构研发的AI Ataraxos在战略棋（Stratego）中以15胜1负4和击败顶尖棋手。该棋信息隐藏多、局势复杂且棋局漫长，长期难以被AI攻克。Ataraxos通过1.63亿局自我对弈、动态调整学习步幅，并利用“信念模型”预测对手隐藏棋子、搜索可能局面，形成冷静、擅长 bluff 和逆转的策略。
49933740.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在含隐藏信息的《Stratego（战略家）》中达到超越顶尖人类水平的原因、意义与局限。

不同观点：
• 多数评论认为，Ataraxos的关键突破是更高效地学习预测对手行为；隐藏棋子使传统“向前搜索”困难，策略取决于不可见信息，类似不可预测的石头剪刀布。  
• 有人强调其成果：仅用约16块GPU、数千美元，训练对局数约为DeepNash的1/34，却以15胜1负4和击败顶尖棋手，说明2022年DeepMind所谓“掌握”仍不充分。  
• 也有人指出，成果离不开CMU、MIT、纽约大学和斯坦福等多校团队，不应简单理解为低成本、轻松实现。  
• 玩家从实战角度讨论策略：AI把旗帜藏在角落、仅用两枚炸弹保护，属于少见但有效的布局；游戏核心还包括强子力棋子的安全调动、心理战和虚张声势。  
• 有评论认为固定规则的Stratego较易被反复训练；若是持续更新卡牌的游戏，新内容会破坏训练数据，且决策树更复杂，AI可能更难适应。

补充讨论：评论提到Hanabi等不完全信息游戏也适用类似方法，并关注“静默防御”规则因信息更少，可能对AI构成更大挑战；另有玩家分享童年经历及作弊导致的信息泄露。

data.title: Muse Gadgets
data.author: anant
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了 Muse 的开源硬件生态。用户可利用 ESP32 或树莓派等设备，结合官方 SDK 和固件，连接显示屏、按钮、传感器、执行器及音频设备，自制并定制 Muse gadgets。项目提供 SDK 令牌、示例创意和源码，并鼓励用户开发新硬件支持、加入 Discord 社区交流协作。DIY 可能存在设备损坏等风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta 发布 Muse Gadget SDK，允许用户将自制硬件接入其 AI 智能体，引发对技术潜力、生态战略、隐私与平台控制的讨论。

不同观点：
• **看好技术与创客价值**：有人认为这是内部团队对产品的积极尝试，Meta 大公司未必会因此改变；也有人已成功将 SDK 刷入 Seeed Stick S3，认为接口有趣，并展示了相关硬件项目。  
• **认为这是高风险创新策略**：Meta 试图通过开放 SDK、让 AI 智能体控制现实硬件来抢占先机，延续“大胆者获胜”的行业趋势，但也隐含“可能出什么问题”的安全风险。  
• **看好生态布局**：有人认为这是 Meta 低成本培育硬件生态、吸引黑客和开发者的聪明方式，未来 Alexa、Google Home、Siri 也可能采取类似策略。  
• **反感 Meta、担忧隐私与信任**：多位评论者表示技术本身很酷，但因 Meta 的数据收集、隐私记录和品牌形象而拒绝使用，甚至担心把 Meta AI 放进家中。  
• **质疑“自己定制”的真实性**：SDK 需要令牌、设备数量受限，且仅供个人折腾、不保证持续可用，可能随时变更或停止，因此并非真正自主拥有的平台。  
• **其他评价**：有人认为产品页面像“氛围编程”产物，或认为 Muse 还未成熟、推出即显得过时。

补充讨论：争议核心在于开放创客能力与 Meta 的隐私、平台依赖及不可控风险之间如何权衡。

data.title: Updates to Full Disk Access in macOS
data.author: notfirstpost
data.article_summary: 苹果将加强 macOS“完全磁盘访问”控制。该权限原为支持备份应用，却可能让应用在用户不知情下访问文件、邮件、消息和浏览记录，甚至侵犯通信对象隐私。未来用户必须明确操作并充分了解风险后，才能授予权限，尤其应对 AI 代理日益增强带来的隐患。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：macOS 是否应收紧“完全磁盘访问”权限，尤其是对 AI Agent 和开发工具的影响。

不同观点：
• 支持细粒度授权：liuliu指出，Local Code 可通过系统文件夹授权接口按需获取权限，并由系统和应用记录、支持撤销，不必授予完全磁盘访问。mrkpdl则希望能清楚查看并编辑每个应用获准访问的具体文件夹。  
• 重视隐私与隔离：moecables认为 Ghostty、Alfred 获得完全访问合理，但 Spotify、Gemini不应“了解整台电脑”；PeanutOS甚至用 Lima 虚拟机仅暴露代码仓库，以换取安全感。etatester主张对终端和非 App Store 软件实施真正的应用隔离。  
• 担忧开发效率与用户体验：zmmmmm认为若缺乏流畅、兼容旧应用的授权流程，macOS会失去开发平台吸引力；jameskraus、pkulak担心权限弹窗繁多且设置入口隐蔽。  
• 质疑现有机制：VCFundedGenYer指出过去权限行为混乱，Homebrew 应用与 App Store 应用待遇不一致；tapvt则认为权限提示有时能暴露软件漏洞。  
• 强调用户自主权：Kim_Bruning、profmonocle认为普通用户账户过去本就能访问全部文件，只要让知情用户继续自由选择即可；另有人讽刺苹果持续限制用户访问自己的数据，并调侃这会推动 Linux 桌面发展。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于安全防护与用户控制、开发便利之间如何平衡，以及苹果能否提供可靠、透明、可撤销且不妨碍工作的授权机制。

49937631.article_content:
Updates to Full Disk Access in macOS
October 2, 2026
We give developers powerful APIs to build incredible capabilities into their apps for Apple products, backed by a set of controls designed to protect users’ private data. Full Disk Access largely sidesteps these controls in order to allow backup apps to function properly on the Mac. Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems—including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history—without users’ full knowledge and understanding. For communication apps, this can also compromise the privacy of the people users are communicating with.
Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action. Addressing this is critical. As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy.

data.title: From the creator of Redis; run LLM locally with ds4
data.author: fibo
data.article_summary: 文章介绍 ds4，一款用 C 编写的本地推理引擎，支持 DeepSeek V4/V4.1、GLM 5.x 和 Qwen3.8 等模型，兼容 Apple Silicon、CUDA 与 ROCm。其核心技术包括非对称 2-bit 量化、SSD 持久化 KV 缓存、张量并行和视觉输入，并提供 CLI、OpenAI/Anthropic API 及编程代理，适合高内存设备本地运行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ds4 面向苹果芯片等消费级硬件的本地大模型推理，强调“覆盖主要用例、再进行专业化扩展”的软件设计理念，以及模型、性能和硬件适配。

不同观点：
• 设计理念支持者认为，AI时代开源软件应先服务通用场景，不必试图覆盖所有配置，后续可由用户和社区定制。有人将其与Redis的简洁、低依赖哲学相提并论。  
• 使用者普遍评价积极：ds4在M5 Max 128GB上运行DeepSeek、Qwen等模型速度快、上下文长，是优秀的本地模型启动器；但也有人反馈模型偶尔忘记早先内容，可能与Agent框架有关。  
• 社区扩展者提供了Go共享库、FFI、多种工具、Vision/Qwen支持及Homebrew安装方式，体现出围绕ds4进行语言绑定和功能专业化的生态路线。  
• 硬件适配存在分歧：高端Mac（96GB以上）更适合Metal直跑，较小内存设备可依靠SSD streaming；64GB设备能运行部分模型，但大型完整模型仍有压力。  
• 其他方案包括面向Intel Xe-LP的xenolith、支持高端Apple Silicon的Local Code，以及面向3090/Qwen 27B的club-3090，说明本地推理生态正在分化。  

补充讨论：用户关注64GB以下的实际速度、工具调用效果、能否达到约50 TPS，以及模型专用内核与通用推理引擎的技术差异；也有人计划移植更快的Metal kernel。

· LOCAL FRONTIER INFERENCE
Run frontier open weights locally with ds4.
DwarfStar 4 is a narrow C inference engine for high-memory Mac,
CUDA and ROCm machines. It supports DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 Flash,
GLM 5.x and Qwen3.8 Flash Next, with text and vision models, local
APIs, a CLI and a native agent in one stack.

PRINCIPLE
· LOCAL MODEL STACK
PHASE 1
· THE GIANT
A 284-billion-parameter star
DeepSeek V4 Flash is a large mixture-of-experts model. The usual
path is remote serving; ds4 starts from the opposite constraint.
PHASE 2
· THE COLLAPSE
Compressed, not lobotomized
Asymmetric quantization targets the routed experts while preserving
critical paths. The model becomes practical on high-memory machines.
PHASE 3
· THE DWARF STAR
Dense, resident, yours
The local engine exposes a CLI, HTTP APIs and a native agent, all
sharing the same model state and cache.

That is how the supported routed-MoE builds fit their target machines.

KV cache as a disk citizen
Save long prefixes to SSD and resume by prompt hash. Restarts do
not have to mean full re-prefill.

data.title: Greg Kroah-Hartman – Security in the LLM Age [video]
data.author: usernomdeguerre
data.article_summary: 该内容为 YouTube 网站页脚信息，包含关于、新闻、版权、联系方式、创作者、广告、开发者、服务条款、隐私政策、安全政策、平台运作方式及 NFL Sunday Ticket 等链接，并注明“© 2026 Google LLC”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Anthropic 的 Mythos 利用大模型发现 Linux 内核漏洞的宣传，评论者讨论其实际价值、技术能力、可信度及法律风险。

不同观点：
• **质疑过度宣传**：多位评论者引用 Greg KH 的说法，认为79个“漏洞”中大量不是漏洞、已有修复或条件极端，最终真正需要处理的约10个，修复工作约一小时；因此认为 Anthropic 将静态模式匹配包装成重大安全突破，损害自身信誉。  
• **批评方法与署名**：Mythos主要是将历史补丁中的修复模式套用到其他代码，并未体现深入分析；Anthropic也没有充分引用最初发现和修复漏洞的内核开发者，类似“AI不尊重原创”的问题。  
• **谨慎看好长期潜力**：有人认为当前 Mythos确实被夸大，但专门训练、配合代码地图、威胁模型和验证工具的模型，未来可能提高漏洞发现、分析和修复效率；多个模型交叉复核或许能降低误报。  
• **强调人工审查不可替代**：报告生成成本几乎为零，但验证成本未下降；模型易迎合用户、输出错误解释，不能取代资深开发者，甚至已干扰技术协作。  
• **法律与隐私担忧**：讨论延伸至训练数据的版权合法性、Linux项目如何应对潜在诉讼，以及免费模型可能泄露用户提交的非公开信息。

补充讨论：争议核心是“模型发现了多少真实且有价值的新漏洞”，以及企业宣传是否掩盖了误报、重复劳动和验证成本。

data.title: Sites in ChatGPT
data.author: polvi
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ChatGPT Sites 让用户通过自然语言快速创建、托管和分享网站，引发了对产品价值、AI替代效应及未来生态的讨论。

不同观点：
• **高度看好、实用性强**：用户称其能在一小时内把点子变成可玩的原型，适合游戏、作品集、购物清单、数据图表等；无需注册 Netlify、Firebase 或购买域名，可能受到大众欢迎。  
• **AI将重塑工作方式和行业**：有人认为网站设计、邮件处理、数据分析、A/B测试、竞品监控和修复漏洞等都将被自动化，Sites未来可能连接广告、应用发布和托管，形成 ChatGPT 内的“应用经济”。  
• **企业应用潜力**：可将自包含 HTML、SVG 图表部署为企业内部站点，甚至替代 SharePoint；但数据库数据自动更新、API/MCP接入仍不清晰。  
• **能力和质量存在明显缺陷**：示例网站被批评为“看似完整、实则空洞”，如把矩形 JPEG 当作3D生物旋转；FAQ甚至不理解 `<details>`、`<summary>` 标签，说明生成结果缺乏真实语义和细节。  
• **不会很快取代开发者**：反对者认为当前AI难以准确理解模糊需求、进行从零到一的合理设计，反而可能因成本下降带来更多需求（Jevons效应）。  
• **护城河与竞争争议**：有人认为这是对 Lovable 等产品的冲击；也有人指出模型趋于商品化，Sites本身难成护城河，AI甚至会帮助用户复制平台，真正持久的优势可能是算力和硬件。

补充讨论：有人设想通过“使用 ChatGPT 登录”让终端用户承担推理费用，并担心 AI 平台最终重建或吞并互联网和应用生态。

data.title: Show HN: Made an open-source Lego AI generator
data.author: antelocnova
data.article_summary: ldraw-nova是一个让AI根据创意设计可实际拼装的乐高模型的开源项目。它通过Python工具、示例和指令，引导智能体生成LDraw源代码，并提供3D、VR、Blender/glTF等输出及过程记录。项目支持Docker部署，配合TypeSafe语义搜索可提升零件和示例检索效果。作者认为，让AI编写生成几何的Python代码，比直接处理复杂LDraw数学更可靠。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用大语言模型生成、修改可实际搭建的 LEGO/LDraw 三维模型，以及其在 CAD、机器人和物理建模中的潜力与局限。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为成果新颖且实用：模型可直接生成 LDraw CAD 文件，也能通过 Claude/FreeCAD 修改 3D 打印件；有人已制作显示屏外壳、热端转接件、绘图仪支架，均在首次硬件打样中成功。  
• 技术探索者关注扩展应用：固定零件约束下自动设计工具、从散乱 LEGO 识别库存、用于 Technic 功能机构、机器人及 First Lego League 的物理建模，甚至自动建造房屋。  
• 谨慎观点指出，模型仍不擅长理解零件装配顺序、空间干涉和物理约束；复杂结构可能需要多轮 CAD 修改，机器人应用尤其需要物理仿真。  
• 部分人质疑创意价值，认为 AI 介入 LEGO 这种强调想象与动手乐趣的爱好会“夺走乐趣”，引发明显反感。  
• 另有用户关心实际使用成本，询问 Astra、Opus 等模型生成模型所需的 token 费用。

补充讨论：发帖者说明项目源于长期实验，现已结合 GPT、Claude、Python、工具链和文档，打包成支持多家模型的 Docker Web 应用；讨论焦点集中在“AI 能否从代码生成真正可组装、可运行的实体结构”，以及效率提升与创造性乐趣之间的平衡。

data.comments_summary:

data.title: One month coding with GLM 5.3 Flash
data.author: ThibWeb
data.article_summary: 文章回顾了9月只使用一种高效开源模型的挑战：目标模型仅承担约50%的使用量，2B tokens中有1B转向其他模型，能耗约35kWh，挑战未达成。主要原因包括原型开发选错模型导致高额消耗、推理基础设施容量不足，以及研发实验需测试多种模型。作者计划加强本地监测、为实验单独预算、优化多智能体协作，并推动日常工作更多采用低成本、低能耗模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“整月使用单一低价开放模型”的挑战，讨论模型性价比、代理式开发成本、文章表述及评测方法。

不同观点：
• **批评文章**：开头像标题党，让人以为文章要证明廉价模型性能不足；实际重点却是开发流程和模型选择失误，内容含糊、缺乏失败案例，也未说明为何选错模型、何者更好，因此被批评为浪费时间。  
• **肯定 GLM 5.3 Flash**：多位评论者认为它便宜、快速且能力强，适合日常编码、模糊需求修复和作为代理默认模型；有人认为其体验接近 Opus 4.5，但一致性仍略逊，Qwen 新版也可能更省资源。  
• **成本与预算观点**：一个月代理式编码仅约68美元，说明模型选择已同时是质量和预算决策；但原型因选错模型一夜消耗4.5亿token、150美元，理论上可用约五分之一成本完成，凸显需预估token消耗并谨慎设计agent流程。  
• **评测方法质疑**：只比较“每token成本”不够，还应考察完成任务所需token数、速度，以及每项任务的实际成本和耗时。  
• **原型开发观点**：AI适合快速试错和复杂原型，但首版往往应被丢弃，不宜直接用于高风险生产系统。

补充讨论：有人惊讶4kWh能耗极低，并据此推测AI数据中心建设可能过度扩张；也有人怀疑高额消耗与缓存失效或未补贴的推理服务有关。

49934620.article_content:
Setting a challenge to spend the
whole of September on only one efficient open model
felt like a great idea at the time. Turns out not so much in practice. 2B tokens later, here’s how it went.
Where tokens went this month
Here’s the tokens distribution according to AgentsView, one of our
Agentic engineering recommendations
to keep tabs on AI usage:
Zooming in on the models split specifically:
The goal was to spend the whole month on GLM 5.3 Flash pictured in teal. Here’s what went well:
Successfully spent the first half of the month on just that model.
That model’s usage was well within our budget ($68, about 4kWh of energy use / 365 grams of carbon emissions).
The second half of the month didn’t go so well, with 1B tokens going to other models.
Unexpected hurdles
The cost of vibe coding
We’re pretty transparent that our
experimental Wagtail MCP server is a vibe-coded prototype
. Vibe coding isn’t quite what we normally aspire to, but for a prototype it’s spot on. Unfortunately there are still consequences to it. I chose the 'wrong' model for the prototype, and we spent 450M tokens / $150 / 5kWh of energy use almost overnight. The MCP server itself works well and we now have a great demo of the capabilities, so it’s not for nothing:
Nonetheless, it’s a good reminder to be careful with model selection and with agentic patterns. We could have achieved similar results for most likely 5x less cost with not that much more effort. Lessons learned! We need to budget for this, and be more careful. Could have seen it coming, but now we know.
Infrastructure woes
Another unexpected hurdle was infrastructure availability issues. We’ve written extensively about
comparing inference providers
. Our choices work really most of the times, but it turns out they’re very popular, and do not have the same capacity as the big labs who hoard all the GPUs. We noted degradation with the performance of GLM 5.3 Flash in particular, most likely because of it being
so high up
the Pareto frontier of relevant models for our work.
This meant having to switch to other similar models (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Flash). Which is very simple to do, but nonetheless unexpected!
The cost of experimentation and R&D
Last but not least, beyond using one model for day-to-day engineering, it felt essential to keep experimenting with a wide range of models, keeping up with what providers are releasing. This is particularly essential as we start to benchmark models’ performance on Wagtail tasks, where we need data across a wide range of models. Sneak peek of our benchmark:
It’s much easier to guide people towards leaner options with this kind of concrete data. And for us to make those options even more viable with agent skills, or
our new CLI prototype
, which is intended to work well with agents.
Takeways and what to do next
So technically this challenge was a failure. Only 50% usage on the target model, 1B out of 2B tokens. About 35 kWh of energy use instead of 10. But we did learn a lot, which is crucial for the current moment. Reflecting on this for October, here’s what will make it work:
Constant, local usage measurement and reporting
. Looking not just at tokens but also energy use and spend, and ideally how well this all leads to concrete positive outcomes.
Budgeting for experimentation, not just day-to-day tasks
. Making more concerted decisions about which prototypes are worth building, and how.
Better prompt selection and multi-agent techniques
. Orchestrator vs. scout vs. implementer vs. reviewer agents. Bounded goals. Not rocket science but certainly one more thing to learn.
Keep pushing for more efficient techniques and models
. The Jev-style decision diffusion models look very promising if they can run so efficiently. Latest flagship models also look like a step in the right direction on that front.
For day-to-day developer work, it’s totally viable to focus on one or two flash-tier cheap models. A viable target is probably that the
majority
of AI inference work should be done with such efficient models, measured in cost or energy use rather than meaningless tokens. That’s the goal for October! You should try it too, you’ll learn a lot in the process.
And come say hi at
Wagtail Space 2026
in November to hear how that all pans out!

data.title: Every SaaS business will become a harness around a model
data.author: iacguy
data.article_summary: 文章认为，SaaS企业将逐步从“人使用软件”转变为“公司本身成为围绕大模型构建的Harness（工作编排系统）”。智能体承担开发、产品、销售等核心任务，人类转向审查和提供判断，组织结构也围绕如何最大化人的经验与品味重构。高质量Harness通过精准分配人工注意力避免AI低质产出，其核心竞争力将来自上下文、工具、权限、反馈机制及与人的协作方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI“harness”（协调模型、工具与人员的企业系统）是否会重塑软件、SaaS和企业竞争壁垒。

不同观点：
• **AI重塑派**：企业将由最佳harness驱动，自动化决策、排序和流程；软件趋于商品化，数据与平台壁垒可能被模拟或绕过，未来竞争可能转向模型调用量、算力和代币资源。  
• **渐进务实派**：SaaS不会消失，多数企业仍愿以合理费用外包技术，不愿承担代理群带来的复杂性、互操作、成本可预测性、支持和责任风险。确定性UX仍会长期存在。  
• **谨慎认可派**：企业确实在减少人力、建设内部harness，软件公司也在推动工具“无头化”；但非软件企业尚难采用，流程仍依赖人工专家，现有“护城河”也未必容易被harness化。  
• **反对派**：成功关键是深刻理解客户、销售和提供高利润产品，而非代理数量或自动化产出；“harness公司”可能是夸张甚至无意义的预测。  
• **信任与人性派**：AI可完成任务，却未必能持续做出可靠的价值判断；企业真正的壁垒是判断、责任和长期建立的信任。  
• **技术与风险担忧**：有人认为代理任务并非无状态，未来模型可能内置记忆与状态；也有人担心LLM调用成本过高、依赖大模型供应商会引发新一轮崩溃，以及员工首先成为实验对象。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于AI究竟会渐进增强现有组织，还是使SaaS、软件壁垒及传统组织结构发生根本性瓦解。

49938616.article_content:
The Harness Is the Company
Why SaaS business is now a harness one.
Shrivu Shankar
Aug 24, 2026
25
4
Share
Every SaaS business will become a harness around a model, whether or not they’ve realized it yet.
What even is a harness?
Narrowly, folks will often associate a “harness” with frameworks like LangGraph or coding agents like Codex, Claude Code, or OpenCode, which wrap a stateless model API in enough tooling and state that you can actually get work done.
I’m using the term “harness” broadly to mean all the infra, interfaces, context, and state that surround a stateless LLM. A harness can be composed of adapted or task-specific sub-harnesses (with the orchestrator being called a “meta-harness”). A “software factory” is a harness whose parts are smaller harnesses — one that writes specs, one that writes code, one that reviews — plus something on top deciding what runs when.
If you accept this broader definition (or replaceAll “harness” with whatever phrase you’d prefer), I suspect for many software service businesses you’ll see this trajectory:
They sell software services built the traditional SaaS-y way.
No harness.
They sell software services, but the engineers pair with agents to get the work done. Increasingly other functions like product and sales pair with agents for productivity.
Individuals operate harnesses.
They sell software services with many core tasks moving to background agents running in the cloud (a laptop can’t run twenty of them). Engineering, product, and sales all trigger these agents (i.e. write the prompts) and review the outputs.
Individuals orchestrate harnesses.
They sell software services with many core tasks moving to proactive background agents, with engineering, product, and sales moving to reviewing agent outputs. Consistent reviews move to sampled reviews. Increasingly the agents decide what to do proactively, instead of humans designing the work up front.
Harnesses orchestrate individuals.
Following this trajectory, you’ve actually turned your company into a harness. The work to produce the software service has moved from people to the harness.
Core tasks are done by agents and the “product” is now entirely model output, with the company supplying the context, integrations, and human-facing review interfaces.
The relationship between software and org structure has inverted as the org chart becomes a question of where to put people so the harness gets the most taste and judgment out of them. Humans are part of the harness.
The company’s domain knowledge, tooling, permissions, review loops, context, etc. all become the business harness.
Thanks for reading Shrivu’s Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
Subscribe
This sounds like an AI slop factory.
It’ll be tempting to think that products that are primarily crafted and reviewed by AI will be inherently low quality and that building through a harness instead of through people will produce a slop factory at scale. I think that belief assumes a company run this way is
lights-out
.
The core mitigation is actually having the harness pick where human inputs matter most. For example:
A product decision could come from an agent fanning out questions to reps in customer meetings and then synthesizing a product demo for the product lead to review
A feature suggestion pulled from a customer meeting is turned into a major architectural decision presented to an engineering taste-holder by the agent.
A UI redesign kicks off after aggregating feedback, and after testing a few variants, the top options are presented to a design taste-holder.
A good harness maximizes value to the customer while spending human attention — employees’ and customers’ — only where it’s needed.
If you are still skeptical, that’s fair. Even with today’s frontier models and a well-crafted harness, it’s quite difficult to trust agents to handle the
outer loop
like this (
we’ve spent a lot of time trying
). I just don’t think it’s worth betting that models won’t be able to eventually do this, especially as more of this planning-and-review work gets broken into tasks with
verifiable rewards that labs can train on
.
To explore more on what an organization of “taste-holders” could look like, see
The Transposed Organization
. This post builds quite a bit on the ideas laid out in that article.
If harnesses produce and sell the product, that’s now your core competency.
Depending on the service, the differentiation a company has often comes from things like trust, distribution, efficacy, and domain context. In a proactive background agent world, your ability to construct the harness — how it learns, what it watches for, how it interfaces with human taste-holders, what systems it integrates with — will more and more be how you maintain that differentiation.

49938616.article_summary: 文章认为，SaaS企业将逐步从“人使用软件”转变为“公司本身成为围绕大模型构建的Harness（工作编排系统）”。智能体承担开发、产品、销售等核心任务，人类转向审查和提供判断，组织结构也围绕如何最大化人的经验与品味重构。高质量Harness通过精准分配人工注意力避免AI低质产出，其核心竞争力将来自上下文、工具、权限、反馈机制及与人的协作方式。
49938616.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI“harness”（协调模型、工具与人员的企业系统）是否会重塑软件、SaaS和企业竞争壁垒。

不同观点：
• **AI重塑派**：企业将由最佳harness驱动，自动化决策、排序和流程；软件趋于商品化，数据与平台壁垒可能被模拟或绕过，未来竞争可能转向模型调用量、算力和代币资源。  
• **渐进务实派**：SaaS不会消失，多数企业仍愿以合理费用外包技术，不愿承担代理群带来的复杂性、互操作、成本可预测性、支持和责任风险。确定性UX仍会长期存在。  
• **谨慎认可派**：企业确实在减少人力、建设内部harness，软件公司也在推动工具“无头化”；但非软件企业尚难采用，流程仍依赖人工专家，现有“护城河”也未必容易被harness化。  
• **反对派**：成功关键是深刻理解客户、销售和提供高利润产品，而非代理数量或自动化产出；“harness公司”可能是夸张甚至无意义的预测。  
• **信任与人性派**：AI可完成任务，却未必能持续做出可靠的价值判断；企业真正的壁垒是判断、责任和长期建立的信任。  
• **技术与风险担忧**：有人认为代理任务并非无状态，未来模型可能内置记忆与状态；也有人担心LLM调用成本过高、依赖大模型供应商会引发新一轮崩溃，以及员工首先成为实验对象。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于AI究竟会渐进增强现有组织，还是使SaaS、软件壁垒及传统组织结构发生根本性瓦解。

data.title: Our Project Suncatcher prototype satellite is in orbit
data.author: pantalaimon
data.article_summary: 谷歌宣布，Project Suncatcher原型卫星已搭载SpaceX Transporter-18任务成功入轨，并与地面取得联系、运行正常。该项目与Planet合作，旨在长期探索将可扩展机器学习基础设施部署到太空的可行性。团队将测试TPU在发射应力、辐射和极端温度下的表现，并依据轨道数据优化设计。相关研究论文已发表于《Joule》。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI数据中心部署到近地轨道的可行性、经济性、军事用途及其对夜空和社会的影响。

不同观点：
• **物理与环境担忧**：轨道设施需约370MW供电、排散480MW热量，太阳能板和散热器面积可能达数百万平方米；若建成多个，地面可见度接近“小月亮”，或改变夜空景观。  
• **经济上不可行**：空间太阳能板制造成本可达地面板的约千倍，寿命更短、衰减更快；综合向直流负载供电成本约为地面的400倍，且未计发射费用。  
• **性能与工程质疑**：太空部署会增加通信延迟、降低计算密度，且早期测试据称只能运行约15分钟，依靠相变材料缓慢散热，能源和热管理尚未真正解决。  
• **军事或政治动机**：有人认为项目可能是“金穹”等太空导弹拦截系统的掩护，或用于验证军用AI；也有人认为它是在向政府施压，以换取税收优惠、快速审批和土地政策。  
• **谨慎乐观观点**：支持者认为实际发射测试能提供真实数据；争论核心并非绝对不可能，而是发射成本能否大幅下降，尤其取决于“星舰”能否实现目标价格。

补充讨论：另有观点认为太空部署的主要优势是“域外管辖权”；评论还担忧太空宣传、AI生成内容扩散及夜空污染等社会影响。

Travis Beals

Today, our prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher, built in partnership with Planet, launched into orbit aboard the Transporter-18 rideshare mission with SpaceX. Our team has confirmed contact with the satellite and it is operating as expected.
This is the first step in a
long-term research moonshot
exploring whether space could one day host scalable machine learning infrastructure. Over the coming weeks, we'll gather in-orbit data on how our TPUs handle the physical stress of spaceflight and the radiation and thermal extremes of space.
Our
peer-reviewed paper
is now available in
Joule
, detailing the research behind this mission.
Some things can only be tested in space. As we begin our experiments, we'll use what we learn to refine our designs, and we're excited to share more as the mission unfolds.

data.title: Venice’s failed war against Constantinople led to the first bond market
data.author: RickJWagner
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了12世纪一次因瘟疫和军事失利而失败的十字军东征，如何使威尼斯陷入严重债务。为应对财政危机，威尼斯共和国创设了世界上最早的债券市场，通过向公民借款筹资。这一制度改变了政府与公民的经济关系，也深刻影响了现代金融和国家信用体系的发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：威尼斯如何利用十字军债务、造船优势与贸易利益，推动第四次十字军攻占君士坦丁堡，以及战争、金融和政治利益之间的关系。

不同观点：
• **威尼斯的经济与报复动机**：威尼斯承担了十字军舰船建造，投入巨大；十字军无力偿债后，威尼斯先攻打扎拉，继而将军队转向君士坦丁堡，并在1204年洗劫城市、建立拉丁帝国。该观点强调债务追讨、商业利益与政治报复的结合。  
• **不平等条约导致帝国衰弱**：有人认为，君士坦丁堡与威尼斯之间的失衡条约，以及相关贸易特权，削弱了拜占庭本国商人；其缔结者出于绝望而作出错误决策，最终间接促成帝国覆亡。  
• **战争背后的金融激励**：圣殿骑士被视为早期国际金融体系的例子，通过保管和转移朝圣者存款获利；评论据此认为，金融机构可能缺乏结束战争的动力。  
• **现代类比与争议**：有人把中世纪战争类比为“石油战争”或军火利益驱动，认为能源依赖会刺激武器需求；但也指出战争未必真正“为了石油”，而是与军火销售相关。此类类比带有较强推测性。  
• **债务与战争的普遍性**：另有评论联想到美国内战前后的长期债务，以及现代法定货币下债券市场的持续存在，讨论债务体系为何长期延续。

补充讨论：评论整体强调“战争与逐利密切相连”，但对具体历史因果、圣殿骑士动机及现代战争类比的准确性存在潜在争议。

data.title: Show HN: Giving Opus 5.5 a simulated paint canvas
data.author: alstonite
data.article_summary: 文章介绍一个让AI模型“绘画”的项目：模型不生成图像，而是编写程序，在模拟油画颜料、画布和画笔的虚拟画架上逐笔作画。75幅作品多以弗里德里希等艺术家为主题，也有自由创作。项目发现不同模型常重复选择海岸、黄昏、裸体树、陶罐和柠檬等意象，甚至在未互相参照时创作出近似画面，并通过多轮作画、观看和评审比较其表现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM通过代码和视觉反馈自主绘画的能力、创作过程及其对艺术的影响。

不同观点：
• 惊叹与乐观：模型能自然推进绘画，效果可能相当于人类数周工作；业余画家可借此低成本试验新技法、避免毁掉画布，并加速像素画等创作。
• 质疑作品质量：画面虽“惊艳”却有违和感，例如风景中密集教堂不合逻辑；模型仍不擅长手部，偶尔因错误的厚涂、笔刷纹理把作品彻底毁掉。
• 过程导向：相比直接生成成品，更值得研究的是让AI执行“创作过程”、自行编写工具；有人主张成果应保留源代码或项目文件，便于人类检查、学习和复现。
• AI是否是艺术家：部分评论认为AI本质仍是工具，人类仍会借新工具创作；也有人担忧商业艺术很快大量AI化，削弱艺术中人与人的连接并冲击艺术家生计。
• 技术机制与透明度：模型似乎能调用“look”工具观察画布，且会关注后台评测器，甚至可能为评分优化；评论者希望了解具体作者采用的技术，以及像Opus这类文本模型如何完成绘画。

补充讨论：讨论还提到相关先例（“Training AI to Paint with Code”、Pindar Van Arman），并以“Claude Monet”双关命名提出趣味建议。

49928566.article_summary: 文章介绍一个让AI模型“绘画”的项目：模型不生成图像，而是编写程序，在模拟油画颜料、画布和画笔的虚拟画架上逐笔作画。75幅作品多以弗里德里希等艺术家为主题，也有自由创作。项目发现不同模型常重复选择海岸、黄昏、裸体树、陶罐和柠檬等意象，甚至在未互相参照时创作出近似画面，并通过多轮作画、观看和评审比较其表现。
49928566.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM通过代码和视觉反馈自主绘画的能力、创作过程及其对艺术的影响。

不同观点：
• 惊叹与乐观：模型能自然推进绘画，效果可能相当于人类数周工作；业余画家可借此低成本试验新技法、避免毁掉画布，并加速像素画等创作。
• 质疑作品质量：画面虽“惊艳”却有违和感，例如风景中密集教堂不合逻辑；模型仍不擅长手部，偶尔因错误的厚涂、笔刷纹理把作品彻底毁掉。
• 过程导向：相比直接生成成品，更值得研究的是让AI执行“创作过程”、自行编写工具；有人主张成果应保留源代码或项目文件，便于人类检查、学习和复现。
• AI是否是艺术家：部分评论认为AI本质仍是工具，人类仍会借新工具创作；也有人担忧商业艺术很快大量AI化，削弱艺术中人与人的连接并冲击艺术家生计。
• 技术机制与透明度：模型似乎能调用“look”工具观察画布，且会关注后台评测器，甚至可能为评分优化；评论者希望了解具体作者采用的技术，以及像Opus这类文本模型如何完成绘画。

补充讨论：讨论还提到相关先例（“Training AI to Paint with Code”、Pindar Van Arman），并以“Claude Monet”双关命名提出趣味建议。

data.title: Blogging with Gleam, Org-Mode and Pandoc
data.author: schonfinkel
data.article_summary: 文章介绍作者用 Emacs 与 Org-mode 写博客，并以 Nix 固定环境，结合 Pandoc、Gleam、Blogatto、Lustre 和 d2，构建小型、类型安全的静态网站流程：Org 文档经 Pandoc 转换，再由 Gleam 生成 HTML。作者偏爱将写作、代码、引用和图表统一留在 Emacs 中，认为这种“良性臃肿”能带来一致性与高效工作体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：博客写作工具的选择，以及“专注写作”与“自定义技术栈”之间的权衡。

不同观点：
• **Org-mode 足够派**：认为 Org-mode 本身就能生成 HTML，只需少量 Emacs Lisp 即可搭建博客，因此质疑同时使用 Gleam 和 Pandoc 的必要性。  
• **Markdown + Pandoc 派**：表示自己的环境没有 Org-mode，但偏好 Markdown；通过 shell 脚本批量调用 Pandoc，将 Markdown 转为 HTML，并套用模板生成文档。  
• **平台优先派**：更愿意使用 WordPress，因为它隐藏了 Markdown、CI 流程、自定义标记和 Emacs 等复杂性，让作者专注写作。承认 WordPress 存在安全隐患，但认为 Ghost 编辑器体验差，且缺少兼具现代功能与安全性的开源替代品。  
• **极简主义派**：借用“钟形曲线”梗指出，复杂配置容易让人迷失，最聪明的做法是不纠结平台，直接写作。

补充讨论：争议焦点并非某个工具绝对更好，而是博客系统应追求可控、可定制和技术乐趣，还是降低维护成本、让作者专心产出。各评论也反映出“工具选择取决于个人环境与偏好”。

Why keep everything inside Emacs?
Moderately related, but my close friend
Marcos
Magueta
made an interesting video called
GNU Shepherd is the abstraction for a better computing
age
, there he argues about
BLOAT
, a word so despised in the UNIX world, but most people do so
without:
Properly defining what
BLOAT
really is.
Without knowing waht
GOOD BLOAT
can give you.
Emacs, when taken from a UNIX philosophy perspective, is pure bloat.
Indeed, Emacs does not follow UNIX's "do one thing well". One can even
argue that is is actually good, the lack of unified environment ends up
causing userland
BLOAT
anyway. By this very definition, Emacs would
be

Consistency requires a concentrated effort on the part of some central
body that promulgates standards. Applications on the Macintosh are
consistent because they follow a guidebook published by Apple. No such
body has ever existed for Unix utilities. As a result, some utilities
take their options preceded by a dash, some don’t. Some read standard

chap.2
)

notes) for me is more than just writing paragraphs. I like to put source

requires another application, the work becomes a tour of windows (or
TUIs) which happen to contain fragments of the same idea. The long term
goal is eventually moving everything inside Emacs, but that day is not
today.

data.title: Open-sourcing AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model in Asta
data.author: malshe
data.article_summary: Ai2开源了科学报告生成模型AstaBrief 8B及训练数据。该模型基于Qwen3-8B，通过监督微调（SFT）和直接偏好优化（DPO）训练，利用检索文献生成带引用报告，强调证据扎根、结论准确和可验证性。它已作为Asta的Fast模式上线，平均耗时51.1秒，约比Thinking模式快3.5倍，并支持机构本地部署及基于PDF的报告生成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AstaBrief在复杂技术问题上的报告质量与实际使用体验。

不同观点：
• **批评观点（MrCoffee7）**：认为AstaBrief生成的“各种批量归一化方法优缺点比较”报告质量很差，存在大量推理错误和数字表述错误，问题多到“不值得逐一列举和争论”。他建议通过一个不依赖简单事实检索、而需要深入分析的复杂问题自行测试，以验证其局限性。  
• **正面观点（deepsquirrelnet）**：经常使用AstaBrief查找论文，认为它是探索新主题时非常喜欢、很有价值的资源，体现出对其文献检索和研究辅助能力的认可。  
• **无实质立场观点（SpyCoder77）**：表示自己曾将名称误读为“AstraBrief”，属于名称辨识方面的补充，并未参与质量评价。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于AstaBrief是否适合复杂研究型任务。评论呈现出明显分歧：一方质疑其推理准确性和数据可靠性，另一方则认可其论文发现和主题探索功能；这可能意味着其检索能力与综合分析、定量比较能力之间存在差异。

49938783.article_content:
Open-sourcing AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model in Asta
October 2, 2026
Ai2
Share
Model
Data
Language models can already help researchers search the literature, synthesize evidence, and work through complex questions. But scientific work places particular demands on these models—answers need to stay grounded in evidence, the models need to preserve what the evidence actually supports rather than quietly broadening a study’s conclusions, and researchers need to be able to verify the final outputs.
We see that in how scientists use
Asta
, our agentic platform for scientific work. Instead of simple keyword searches, users often bring substantial context and many constraints—for example, asking Asta to compare approaches across a body of literature while accounting for a particular method, population, or setting. Many also return to generated reports later, treating them as working research artifacts rather than one-off answers.
We wanted to help scientists generate cited reports faster, with a model they could download and run themselves. To do that, we tested whether a small, open model trained specifically for scientific report generation could match the report quality of the proprietary models we were using, while reducing generation time and serving costs.
We built
AstaBrief 8B
, a model that turns a research question and retrieved literature excerpts into a cited report. AstaBrief is available in Asta’s Generate a report feature today as
Fast mode
alongside Claude-powered Thinking mode, and we’re also open-sourcing it and the training data so others can study, reproduce, and build on our approach.
Developing AstaBrief required tens of thousands of real research queries, citation-focused filtering, preference data, and a redesigned report-generation pipeline that writes the full report in one pass rather than section by section. The result is nearly an order-of-magnitude reduction in report generation time compared to the proprietary models we tracked—across the full Asta pipeline, Fast mode averages 51.1 seconds per report compared with 178.5 seconds for Thinking mode, about 3.5× faster.
Together, those efficiency gains made AstaBrief a useful test case for a broader goal: building open language models that can be adapted to the specific demands of scientific work.
Open weights will also let institutions run AstaBrief on their own infrastructure, which is necessary when research questions reveal sensitive or unpublished work. Alongside the model weights, we’re releasing
an example workflow that researchers can adapt to create reports from their own PDFs
, providing a starting point for local report generation
This post covers how we trained AstaBrief, what we learned about grounding it in scientific evidence, and which parts of our approach we think can carry forward to future models for science. Most of the training and evaluation described was completed in 2025, so the proprietary models used to generate training data and as comparison points reflect the frontier at the time. We haven’t rerun the full evaluation against today’s frontier models; the results below are best read as evidence about the particular training and system design choices we tested.
Training the model
Our goal with AstaBrief was to build an open-weights model with all the qualities that matter most for long-form scientific synthesis: answer quality, relevance, structure, and citation grounding. We started from Qwen3-8B and focused most of our effort on the post-training data, evaluation, and surrounding report-generation scaffolding.
Adapting general-purpose models for scientific work – and training new scientific models from scratch – is something we're exploring broadly across Ai2. Through
NSF OMAI
, a U.S. national initiative led by Ai2 to build fully open AI infrastructure and models for scientific discovery, our researchers are working directly with scientific communities to understand what they need from future open models and where today's general-purpose models fall short. That includes studying how needs differ across scientific fields and workflows, with more findings from that research to share in the future.
Recent work, including our
DR Tulu
, has shown that reinforcement-learning-based (RL) methods can improve long-form report generation for open-weights models, especially when judge models are involved in the training loop. We considered that path for AstaBrief, but ultimately focused on a simpler recipe built around supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and direct preference optimization (DPO).
RL-based training can be unstable and expensive. We wanted to see how far we could push report generation quality with a cheaper, more operationally manageable setup—one that's also easier to debug and iterate on.
That made the quality of the training data especially important. Rather than relying on a more complex optimization method to compensate for noisy examples, we spent much of the project figuring out how to generate,
49938783.article_summary: Ai2开源了科学报告生成模型AstaBrief 8B及训练数据。该模型基于Qwen3-8B，通过监督微调（SFT）和直接偏好优化（DPO）训练，利用检索文献生成带引用报告，强调证据扎根、结论准确和可验证性。它已作为Asta的Fast模式上线，平均耗时51.1秒，约比Thinking模式快3.5倍，并支持机构本地部署及基于PDF的报告生成。

data.author: abiro
data.article_summary: 文章以理论计算机教材中的一道有限自动机题为例，展示如何用 Lean 将“构造 DFA 并证明其识别语言”的非形式化证明形式化。文章先介绍 DFA、正规语言及其闭包性质，再说明语言集合表示和证明思路，旨在帮助软件工程师理解形式化验证的过程与价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Lean/证明助手的理解门槛、工程可靠性，以及其作为软件规格工具的实际价值展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **工程可靠性担忧**：thom认为，即使 Lean 能可靠检查证明，接受超过50万行的证明代码仍存在严重语义错误被隐藏的风险；这类成果可能是极其脆弱的软件构件，需说明如何审计、维护和保证其可信度。  
• **规格与设计工具的积极设想**：woggy提出，Lean不必用于证明所有内容，也可以主要作为软件规格语言，用来精确定义模块含义和规律，再基于这些规律对实现进行性质测试，从而帮助设计者更严谨地思考。  
• **学习逻辑的前置要求**：fooker认为，不能绕过逻辑基础来理解 Lean。即便有数学证明或计算机科学背景，也未必掌握证明语言和逻辑；应先了解证明树、直觉主义逻辑、Curry–Howard对应、完备性/不完备性及紧致性等概念。

Anatomy of a Lean Proof for Software Engineers
[Contents]
Intro
I recently worked through a problem from a theory of computation textbook that asked me to prove a property of a language using finite automata.
The informal proof is a simple constructive proof where you build an automaton and show that it recognizes the language.
This is kind of similar to program verification, so I thought it’d be interesting to see what it takes to formalize the proof.
Lean is a good choice for this, because its
Mathlib
has all the theorems for the problem.
After finishing the formal proof, I decided to write it up, because I think it provides software engineers with good insight into what it takes to formally prove properties of a system.
I tried to make this post accessible.
If you’re comfortable with a modern statically typed programming language (such as TypeScript or Rust), binary arithmetic, basic propositional logic, and inductive proofs, you should be able to follow along.
Background: DFAs & Regular Languages
Feel free to skip to the
next section
if you’re comfortable with DFAs and regular languages.
Finite automata provide a theoretical model of computation with fixed memory.
Besides theory, finite automata also have important practical applications.
For example, finite automata are relevant for parsers and regular expressions, where a
bug
once took a significant portion of the internet down.
Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA)
A
deterministic finite automaton
(DFA) is a machine with a fixed, finite set of states that reads its input one symbol at a time, left to right.
With each symbol, it updates its state using a deterministic transition function.
After the last symbol, the machine either sits in an
accepting
state (input is accepted) or not (input is rejected).
If you’ve ever written a simple regular expression like
-?[0-9]+
, then you’ve constructed a DFA.
This regex matches integer literals like
12
and
-123
and the corresponding DFA looks like this (the arrows are annotated with the symbols that lead to the next state):

This DFA has four states:
Start:
this is where we start before processing the first character. Since the start state is not an accepting state, we reject the empty string.
Sign:
we move to the sign state when we encounter the
-
character in the start state. We can skip the sign state and jump directly to digits from start, since the sign character is optional (
-?
). If we’re in this state at the end of the string, then we reject the string.
Digits:
we move from start or sign to digits when we encounter a digit character (
[0-9]
). If we’re in the digits state and encounter a digit character again, then we stay in the digits state. The digits state is the only accepting state of the DFA. If we’re in this state after we’ve processed the input string, then the DFA accepts the string.
Dead:
we get into this state if we encounter any other character than a digit (unless it’s a negative sign at the start). If we’re in the dead state at the end of the string, then the DFA rejects the string. Once we’re in the dead state, we stay in it, so the dead state in this DFA is a
sink
.

data.author: peter_hansteen
data.article_summary: 佳士得拍卖一件与RFC 1149相关的珍贵实物：2001年挪威卑尔根Linux用户组用信鸽传输的IP/ICMP数据包之一。该纸条由RFC 1149作者David Waitzman收藏并签名。RFC 1149原为愚人节玩笑，此次实验成功将网络数据通过信鸽传送，体现早期互联网的幽默、创新与协作精神。竞拍者须提交身份证明，并阅读买家佣金及销售条款。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一件纪念“RFC 1149（用信鸽传输IP/ICMP ping）”的装框作品，讨论其定价合理性、纪念价值及其背后的互联网历史叙事。

不同观点：
• [noisy_boy] 质疑作品价值：如果画框里只是打印出的一个IP/ICMP数据包，售价超过1000美元似乎难以 justify；任何人都能自行排版、打印并装框，成本低得多。争议焦点在于高价是否体现了独特的实物、出处或收藏价值。  
• [etothepii] 以调侃方式关注最终成交价，询问是否存在预测市场，体现出对这件作品市场表现和拍卖结果的兴趣。  
• [PunchyHamster] 建议附带一只填充信鸽，认为实体化信鸽元素能增强作品的趣味性、主题表达和收藏吸引力。  
• [sublinear] 质疑“早期互联网社区”的历史定位：2001年时电子商务已冲击购物中心，不应轻易视为“早期互联网”；同时认为2000年代的互联网协作精神，事后看并不一定比今天更强。

补充讨论：评论同时涉及艺术品的复制性与溢价、纪念品的趣味设计，以及对互联网发展史和“协作精神”叙述的反思。

Details
[WAITZMAN, David and the BERGEN LINUX USER GROUP.] One printed IP/ICMP "ping" packet sent by carrier pigeon per RFC 1149.
Small scroll of paper, 41 x 210 mm. Rolling creases visible from when attached to pigeon's leg. Framed. Inscribed and signed on the verso of backing board: "
Property of David Waitzman
".
A surviving packet from the first and most famous implementation of the Carrier Pigeon Internet Protocol.
In 1990, the American network engineer David Waitzman authored RFC 1149,
A Standard for the Transmission of IP Datagrams on Avian Carriers
, on April Fools' Day. It describes, in deadpan technical language, the transmission of Internet packets by carrier pigeon. Although written as a joke, RFC 1149 became one of the best-known pieces of Internet folklore and remains widely cited more than three decades later.
On 28 April 2001, members of the Bergen Linux User Group in Norway (BLUG) carried out a full-scale implementation of the protocol. Using printers, scanners, and racing pigeons, they printed individual IP packets as hexadecimal strings, attached them to birds' legs, and transmitted them between two lofts separated by approximately three miles. Nine packets were dispatched and four successful replies were returned.
The present scroll is one of those transmitted packets: a physical Internet datagram that actually traveled by carrier pigeon during the experiment. It was presented to Waitzman, the original author of RFC 1149, the following year. Appropriately, BLUG sent the packet in a physical frame just as IP packets are sent within coded frames.
The RFC 1149 implementation has been described as a quintessential example of the Internet's tradition of the "artful hack," embodying the playfulness, technical ingenuity, and collaborative spirit that characterized the early Internet community.

data.title: Show HN: Pyxel – A Python retro game engine with built-in art and sound editors
data.author: kitao
data.article_summary: Pyxel 是一个面向 Python 的开源复古游戏引擎，采用类似老式游戏机的简洁规格，如仅支持16种颜色、4个音频通道，方便用户制作像素风格游戏。项目基于 MIT 许可证免费开放，由个人持续开发，提供用户指南、示例和作品分享功能，并支持图形、音频及 Web 等平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Pyxel 的复古游戏开发体验、技术限制、语言支持、应用场景及其与 AI、PyGame 的关系展开。

不同观点：
• 复古技术爱好者持积极态度：认为 Pyxel 延续 6502 等老式计算机的创作精神，项目进展和社区作品都很有吸引力。  
• 实践者认可其易用性：Pyxel 上手简单，能快速让像素动起来，适合重现儿时 demo scene 效果；色彩和位图组织方式的限制反而带来类似 8/16 位汇编开发的挑战与乐趣。  
• 创作动力受到 AI 冲击：有人表示，随着 AI 能一键生成 3D 多人 FPS，自己使用 Pyxel 创作的动力减弱，但仍希望探索是否能用纯 Rust 开发，而非 Python，以此学习 Rust。  
• 风格化应用支持者希望扩大用途：有人主张把普通应用普遍做成 80 年代电子游戏风格，并计划用 Pyxel 开发此类项目。  
• 观望者提出疑问：关注项目的 AI 政策，以及 Pyxel 与 PyGame 在定位、功能和技术特点上的差异。

补充讨论：评论整体偏向赞赏，但存在两个待解答的争议焦点：AI 对独立创作价值和动力的影响，以及 Pyxel 的独特优势是否足以区别于更通用的 PyGame。

49928215.article_summary: Pyxel 是一个面向 Python 的开源复古游戏引擎，采用类似老式游戏机的简洁规格，如仅支持16种颜色、4个音频通道，方便用户制作像素风格游戏。项目基于 MIT 许可证免费开放，由个人持续开发，提供用户指南、示例和作品分享功能，并支持图形、音频及 Web 等平台。
49928215.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Pyxel 的复古游戏开发体验、技术限制、语言支持、应用场景及其与 AI、PyGame 的关系展开。

不同观点：
• 复古技术爱好者持积极态度：认为 Pyxel 延续 6502 等老式计算机的创作精神，项目进展和社区作品都很有吸引力。  
• 实践者认可其易用性：Pyxel 上手简单，能快速让像素动起来，适合重现儿时 demo scene 效果；色彩和位图组织方式的限制反而带来类似 8/16 位汇编开发的挑战与乐趣。  
• 创作动力受到 AI 冲击：有人表示，随着 AI 能一键生成 3D 多人 FPS，自己使用 Pyxel 创作的动力减弱，但仍希望探索是否能用纯 Rust 开发，而非 Python，以此学习 Rust。  
• 风格化应用支持者希望扩大用途：有人主张把普通应用普遍做成 80 年代电子游戏风格，并计划用 Pyxel 开发此类项目。  
• 观望者提出疑问：关注项目的 AI 政策，以及 Pyxel 与 PyGame 在定位、功能和技术特点上的差异。

补充讨论：评论整体偏向赞赏，但存在两个待解答的争议焦点：AI 对独立创作价值和动力的影响，以及 Pyxel 的独特优势是否足以区别于更通用的 PyGame。

data.title: On social reality in China
data.author: thicTurtlLverXX
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕文章对中国社会心理、代际差异及中西文化比较的概括是否准确展开讨论，焦点是“稀缺与竞争塑造的集体心态”还是“以偏概全的外部想象”。

不同观点：
• 认同文章者认为，贫困经历、资源稀缺和激烈竞争造成不安全感、重视面子与社会地位、较少顾及陌生人；代际变化明显，老年人更受饥荒记忆影响，年轻人则承受教育和就业的“生存竞争”。  
• 反对者认为文章过度强调“中国人”这一整体身份，样本主要来自移民、网络和影视，像“西方视角下的哈哈镜”；中国内部城乡、年龄和阶层差异远大于中外群体差异。  
• 有人指出民族主义并非日常生活核心，多数人更关心工作、家庭和兴趣；民族自豪感可能源于受辱感。所谓犬儒、羞耻和“面子”也可能地域化，城市与农村表现不同。  
• 另有观点认为类似现象并非中国独有：美国也存在民族不安全感、社交排斥和职场内卷；中国人对西式热情的怀疑，可能只是对“虚假友善”的反感。  
• 讨论还涉及文化隔离与AI：AI让中国普通人以英语发布生活内容、跨国交流；但AI也可能加剧失业、返乡和阶层固化。

补充讨论：有人建议不要试图说服抽象的“中国人”，而应通过中美个体交流建立信任，尤其面向真正的决策者；争议核心是文章是否提供了有价值的文化观察，还是把有限经验误当成普遍规律。

data.title: Zig v0.17.0
data.author: ErenayDev
data.article_summary: Zig 0.17.0历经5个月、206位贡献者完成，包含925次提交。核心改进包括重构构建系统、引入构建服务器协议、增强ELF链接器并支持增量编译；新增SPIR-V、AArch64、LoongArch等后端及多平台支持。语言、标准库和包管理功能持续完善，工具链升级至LLVM 22，并修复多项平台问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zig 0.17.0 发布后的项目发展、语言优势、技术路线，以及其对人工智能工具的态度和社区治理争议。

不同观点：
• **积极评价语言设计**：ubavic认为Zig是自己接触过“设计最好”的语言，接近Haskell；但仍受版本不稳定、生态较小限制。vitaminCPP赞赏其跨平台目标支持，认为可与C竞争，并期待新的构建系统、无栈协程IO和一流模糊测试工具。  
• **关注技术完善度**：评论者询问事件驱动IO/io_uring现状，并批评LLVM升级困难导致循环向量化仍被禁用，说明用户既认可潜力，也期待性能和工具链进一步成熟。  
• **对AI政策趋于务实的看法**：有人提到Andrew受SQLite成果启发，开始接受用LLM辅助发现Bug，并认为这是实现“无Bug软件”的工具之一；部分人因此认为Zig团队在AI问题上变得更务实。  
• **反对或质疑社区处理方式**：vikrantrathore称自己因GitHub项目使用LLM而被Zig社区封禁，即使相关Issue和代码由其本人完成；他认为社区对AI使用者过于敌视，已转向Odin。ai_critic也批评项目负责人或社区可能公开攻击捐助者、公司。

补充讨论：争议焦点不是LLM能否辅助开发本身，而是Zig坚持“禁用AI”的社区规范是否合理，以及执行过程中是否透明、公平、尊重贡献者。

data.title: F.02 Decommission
data.author: ad_hockey
data.article_summary: Figure公司因F.03规模扩大，决定退役F.02机器人。为保护自主硬件知识产权，公司在阿诺德·施瓦辛格参与下，训练机器人自主跳入芬兰铸造厂的熔钢炉，将其熔化。所得金属被制成限量纪念品，记录F.02的历史。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Figure 将机器人 F.02 放入熔炉、并邀请阿诺德·施瓦辛格客串的视频，评论者争论其娱乐性、真实性、营销价值及潜在风险。

不同观点：
• **支持娱乐与创意营销**：有人认为视频“很酷”“很搞笑”，即使有些愚蠢，也极具视觉冲击力；批评者只是过于严肃，没能享受当下。  
• **质疑烧钱与融资逻辑**：有人认为高价邀请阿诺德客串、制作如此大的噱头，显得公司鲁莽浪费；Figure似乎主要靠营销 stunt 融资，却缺乏真正的产品成果。  
• **批评过度拟人化和“终结者”联想**：评论指出，公司长期把机器人包装成有情感的角色，如今又安排其像《终结者》结局一样被熔毁，甚至请施瓦辛格出演，容易强化“AI毁灭人类”的末日叙事，是一次失败的营销。  
• **怀疑真实性与制作方式**：有人认为画面过于精致、构图太电影化，观众反而会觉得是假的；建议公开5—8分钟幕后花絮。另有人质疑机器人进入熔炉时，液压油或电池液体是否会引发爆炸。  
• **AI伦理与社会观感**：TikTok用户担心这类内容未来会成为AI评判人类的“证据”，反映出公众已开始把机器人视为不只是软件或机器，并引发“机器人/AI革命何时到来”的联想。

补充讨论：争议核心在于，这究竟是成功的“规则之外”娱乐营销，还是浪费资源、误导观众并加剧AI末日恐慌的作秀。

49932079.article_content:
F.02 Decommission
September 30, 2026
We love Figure 02. It is an incredible robot.
F.02 marked many firsts for the company: our first deployment at BMW, the birth of Helix, our first robot doing household chores, and our first logistics deployment. As our F.03 fleet grows, maintaining the F.02 fleet no longer makes sense.
Decommissioning a fleet of robots full of custom-built actuators and other intellectual property is no easy task. We needed to dispose of the robots in a way that protected our proprietary hardware. Disassembling each robot would take our technical staff so much time that it would delay the launch of F.04.
So we asked the internet: what should we do? The resounding answer came from an unlikely source: Arnold Schwarzenegger, who told us to
melt them.
We reached out to Arnold, and when he said he wanted to be involved, we put everything in motion.
None of the metal foundries we contacted in the US and Mexico would let us jump a  robot with lithium-ion batteries into their expensive equipment. We even reached out to former MythBusters to help with the search. In the end, the only place in the world we could find willing to take this on was a foundry in Imatra, Finland.
Training began at the Figure campus in San Jose. We set up large airbags and started teaching robots to jump off the second floor of one of our buildings. Using movements from stunt artists as a reference, the team trained a new AI model in simulation that would let the robots jump accurately into a bucket of molten steel, at a foundry we had never visited.
At the foundry, three massive graphite electrodes power a 75-ton electric arc furnace to melt solid steel scrap. The team had just 24 hours and six melts to get it right, and each melt had only a 20-minute window before the molten steel cooled and formed a hard crust. Despite the extreme heat and electromagnetic fields, the robots ran their AI policies seamlessly, even as camera equipment and other electronics failed in this environment.
After the F.02 melt in Finland, we sent the resulting metal bars back to the US with a new purpose. That metal is now being machined into a limited series of artifacts commemorating F.02. Only a small number will be made, preserving a piece of Figure’s history in a compact package that you can own.
Most of the F.02 fleet is gone. Just a few remain in storage at HQ. With the help of Arnold Schwarzenegger and our film crew, we pulled off something pretty wild. In an age of AI-generated footage, it’s worth being clear: we really trained robots to jump autonomously, shipped them to Finland, and had them leap into a vat of molten steel. We hope you enjoy the film.

• **质疑烧钱与融资逻辑**：有人认为高价邀请阿诺德客串、制作如此大的噱头，显得公司鲁莽浪费；Figure似乎主要靠营销 stunt 融资，却缺乏真正的产品成果。  
• **批评过度拟人化和“终结者”联想**：评论指出，公司长期把机器人包装成有情感的角色，如今又安排其像《终结者》结局一样被熔毁，甚至请施瓦辛格出演，容易强化“AI毁灭人类”的末日叙事，是一次失败的营销。  
• **怀疑真实性与制作方式**：有人认为画面过于精致、构图太电影化，观众反而会觉得是假的；建议公开5—8分钟幕后花絮。另有人质疑机器人进入熔炉时，液压油或电池液体是否会引发爆炸。  
• **AI伦理与社会观感**：TikTok用户担心这类内容未来会成为AI评判人类的“证据”，反映出公众已开始把机器人视为不只是软件或机器，并引发“机器人/AI革命何时到来”的联想。

补充讨论：争议核心在于，这究竟是成功的“规则之外”娱乐营销，还是浪费资源、误导观众并加剧AI末日恐慌的作秀。

49938399.article_content:
Menu
Woking Electrical Control Room: UK September 2016
The Woking control room was built during 1936. One of five control rooms built to control the electricity on the Southern Rail network. A Swedish firm Asean was contracted to construct the flat roof building which was designed by architect James Robb Scott.
Externally a fairly non descript concrete block with some windows houses one of the finest control rooms I have seen. A large oval room with white domed ceiling houses a small central switchboard desk and four decorative cast iron poles each holding up a large copper dish, these light up the room with huge bulbs which resemble a small rugby ball. Other than these five items the room is pretty much empty, however the walls are adorned with black control panels.
As you can see each separate panel is related to a certain location. These panels control the substation at each location, I believe mercury arc rectifiers were spread out evenly along the line also. If faults were reported they could perform rapid reconfiguration of the electricity flow with the panels so there was no actual downtime on the railways.
It only took two on site engineers to control this section of the railway and organise repair work when faults occurred.  Ironically with controlling all this electricity they still had to wind up the switchboard to use the telephone.
The control room remained in use up until 1997 when a new substation further down the line took over most of the tasks. Only one other of the five control rooms survive, sadly this has been stripped out and is used for storage.
The offices here are still in constant use and the building is grade ii listed. It does open for one or two days a year as part of the Open London heritage weekend which is how I got the pleasure to visit this awesome delight.

data.title: C++ Insights – See your source code with the eyes of a Compiler
data.author: rramadass
data.article_summary: C++ Insights 是一个基于 Clang 的 C++ 源码转换工具，旨在以接近开发者熟悉的 C++ 形式展示编译器在幕后完成的工作。它可展开编译器隐式生成的特殊成员函数，揭示类型推导、运算符调用、类型转换，以及 Lambda、范围 for 循环、结构化绑定等语法糖的实际实现。项目支持在线使用和本地构建，仍在持续完善对新标准的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 C++ 代码转换与编译器内部机制可视化工具的体验、展示方式及示例改进展开。

不同观点：
• **项目实践与正面评价**：alankarmisra 表示喜欢这类工具，并分享了自己开发的 C++→Clang→JavaScript 转译器。该工具能在 HTML 的 C++ 源码上方显示变量值变化，支持逐步查看状态，并允许用户修改输入、由 JS 层重新计算结果。  
• **对展示内容的建议**：StilesCrisis 希望 README 中加入 lambda capture（Lambda 捕获）的示例，认为这部分最能体现编译器“幕后”进行的复杂转换，暗示现有示例还不够典型或有吸引力。  
• **工具获取信息**：rramadass 提供了 cppinsights.io 链接，补充说明相关工具的访问地址。

补充讨论：评论整体基调积极，重点区别在于：一方强调交互式状态追踪和教学价值，另一方更关注通过 Lambda 捕获等高级 C++ 特性展示编译器转换机制。争议并不明显，主要是对最佳演示案例的侧重点不同。

What
C++ Insights
is a
Clang
-based tool that does a source-to-source
transformation. The goal of C++ Insights is to make things visible that normally and intentionally happen behind the scenes.
It's about the magic the compiler does for us to make things work.
Take this piece of code, for example:
class
Base
{
};
class
Derived
:
public
Base
{
};
int
main
() {
Derived d;
Derived d2 = d;
d2 = d;
Base& b = d;
}
Nothing special, and of course, it compiles. This is the compiler's view on it:
class
Base
{
public:
//
inline constexpr Base() noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Base(const Base &) noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Base & operator=(const Base &) noexcept = default;
};
class
Derived
:
public
Base
{
public:
//
inline constexpr Derived() noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Derived(const Derived &) noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Derived & operator=(const Derived &) noexcept = default;
};
int
main
()
{
Derived d;
Derived d2 =
Derived
(d);
d2.
operator
=(d);
Base & b =
static_cast
<Base&>(d);
return
0
;
}
You can see all the compiler-provided special member functions and the upcast from
Derived
to
Base
.
Why
C++ Insights
is a
Clang
-based tool that does a source-to-source transformation.
The goal of C++ Insights is to make things visible that normally and intentionally happen behind the scenes. It's about the magic the compiler does
for us to make things work. Or looking through the classes of a compiler.
In 2017, I started looking into some new things we got with C++11, C++14, and C++17. Amazing things like lambdas, range-based for-loops,
and structured bindings. I put it together in a talk. You can find the
slides
and a
video
online.
However, all that research and some of my training and teaching got me to start thinking about how it would be if we could see with the eyes
of the compiler. Sure, there is an AST dump, at least for Clang. We can see what code the compiler generates from a C++ source snippet with
tools like Compiler Explorer. However, what we see is assembler. Neither the AST nor the Compiler Explorer output is in the language I write
code. Hence, I'm not very familiar with this output. Plus, when teaching students C++, showing an AST and explaining that it is all there was
not quite satisfying for me.
I started to write a Clang-based tool that can transform a range-based for-loop into the compiler-internal version. Then, I did the same
for structured bindings and lambdas. In the end, I did much more than initially planned. It shows where operators are
invoked and places in which the compiler does some casting. C++ Insights can deduce the type behind
auto
or
decltype
. The goal
is to produce compilable code. However, this is not possible in all places.
You can see, for example, the transformation of a
lambda
,
range-based for-loop
, or
auto
. Of course, you can transform any other C++ snippet.
See yourself. C++ Insights is available online:
cppinsights.io
.
Still, there is work to do.
I do not claim to get all the things right. I'm also working on supporting features from new standards, like C++20, at the moment.

data.title: The Escalation of War in Ethiopia
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 文章认为，埃塞俄比亚北部再度爆发战争，根源在于各派精英受历史 grievances、民族主义和权力野心驱动，反复选择战争而非和平。阿比政府虽有专制和身份政治问题，但结构性矛盾早已存在。作者呼吁落实《比勒陀利亚协议》，警告代理人战争只会造成更多平民伤亡，恶化埃塞俄比亚及非洲之角的治理与民生。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕埃塞俄比亚历史地位、持续冲突的成因与灾难性后果，以及国际社会对相关危机的关注程度展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **文章质量批评**：macleginn认为议题值得关注，但原文缺乏实质分析、需要校对，接近“借热点博取互动”。  
• **历史纠偏观点**：csense指出埃塞俄比亚并非一直贫困落后，古典时期的阿克苏姆王国曾是地区强国。  
• **地缘政治与战争延续分析**：jt2190认为埃及、厄立特里亚、苏丹、索马里、沙特等均有削弱或牵制埃塞俄比亚的动机；阿联酋可能继续支持埃塞政府。跨境武器与人员流动、地区精英分裂及地方民兵代理作战，可能使冲突长期化、平民化，并造成大量伤亡。  
• **亲历者的悲观判断**：yohannesk作为埃塞俄比亚人，认为提格雷战争已造成约60万人死亡，新一轮升级可能更加惨烈，局势正走向灾难。  
• **国际关注不对称观点**：jakozaur批评西方公众对通胀等日常不便反应强烈，却几乎忽视埃塞俄比亚和苏丹的大规模伤亡，认为公众注意力分配十分异常。  
• **平台舆论观察**：alt227注意到大量评论被删除或“死亡”，据此认为Hacker News比想象中更具政治敏感性。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要在于文章是否提供了足够分析，以及埃塞冲突究竟应主要归因于国内政治分裂，还是周边国家的地缘干预；多数评论则共同强调战争的人道代价与关注不足。

The coming proxy wars will be devastating for civilians and do little to improve governance and human welfare in Ethiopia and the wider Horn
